| Name the action in sentence case, as a verb and what it acts on: "Show departures", "Show whole line"                                                          | Write "OK", "Click here", Title Case or an exclamation mark ([Content design](../content-design.md))                                              |
| Use IconButton for a button with an icon and no words, so it gets its required label                                                                           | Pass only a `startIcon` and no `children`: the icon is `aria-hidden`, so the button has no name                                                   |
| Use `solid` for the action a panel is for and `outline` for the actions beside it                                                                              | Mark the main action with `outline`, or set every action in a row `solid`                                                                         |
| Set `type="submit"` on a form's submit button; Base UI's default is `type="button"`                                                                            | Rely on a button submitting its form: without `type="submit"` it doesn't                                                                          |
| Pass `nativeButton={false}` with `render` when it gives an element that isn't a `<button>`                                                                     | Render a link with `render={<a href="/map" />}` for navigation: LinkButton is that component, and a button that navigates misleads screen readers |
| Keep a brand button out of rows of line and mode badges                                                                                                        | Set a brand button among bus badges, whose fill and ink label it shares, where it reads as one                                                    |
| Set `disabled` when the action can't run, with a reason in words nearby, or `focusableWhenDisabled` so the button can carry it                                 | Restyle a disabled button with `opacity`: disabled is `color.text.tertiary`, a colour                                                             |

title: IconButton
markdown:
# IconButton

A button that runs one action and shows it as an icon alone, such as zoom in or show help, named for screen readers by its required `label`.

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): there is no read-back, code map or export, and this spec decides what the drawing would, from the contract, the foundations, the tokens, the Base UI reference and the spec of its sibling [Button](button.md), a source it follows rather than a dependency: IconButton builds on Base UI's `Button` and the `VisuallyHidden` part, not on Perron's Button. The [Toolbar](toolbar.md) spec gives its icon-only buttons the look and size answered below, and this spec follows it so the two match side by side.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/IconButton`. Family: none (the contract's [Families](README.md#families) give buttons only their text, and an icon button shows none). Shared parts: `VisuallyHidden`, which holds the label: the contract composes it in "any component with a word the eye gets from an icon or a shape".

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                                                                             | Base UI part                                           | Class                | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | The native `<button>`: a square, `size.control` both ways, that centres the icon                                                                                                       | `Button`                                               | `pn-IconButton`      | none            |
| `icon`              | A `<span>`, `aria-hidden`, that holds the caller's `children`, the icon                                                                                                                | none: a span inside `Button`, which has no inner parts | `pn-IconButton-icon` | none            |
| `label`             | The `VisuallyHidden` span that holds the caller's `label`, the words that name the button. Never seen, so a drawing has no layer for it                                                | none: the `VisuallyHidden` shared part inside `Button` | `pn-VisuallyHidden`  | none            |
| `focusRing`         | The keyboard focus ring, as on Button: the `:focus-visible` outline `perron.css` draws on the root, not an element. A drawing shows it as a layer named `focusRing` on the focus state | `Button`                                               | none                 | none            |

## Base UI parts

Imported from `@base-ui/react/button`, at the version pinned in `package.json` (1.9.0 installed).

| Base UI part | Renders                                                                                     | Perron sets                                                                                                                                                                                      | Passed through                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Button`     | `<button type="button">`, or the element `render` gives, with `data-disabled` when disabled | `className` (`pn-IconButton`, then the caller's), `style`, `ref`, `disabled` from `disabled`, `data-color` and `data-size` from their props (defaults included), and the icon and label children | `render`, `nativeButton`, `focusableWhenDisabled`, `type`, `onClick`, `aria-*` and every other prop of a native `<button>`, through `{...rest}` |

Base UI already does: it renders a native `<button>` with `type="button"`, which a caller's `type="submit"` overrides; Enter and Space activate it through the browser; when disabled it sets the native `disabled` attribute and `data-disabled`, and stops `onClick`, `onMouseDown` and `onPointerDown` from reaching the caller; with `focusableWhenDisabled` it sets `aria-disabled` in place of `disabled`, keeps the button in the tab order and lets only Tab through; with `render` and `nativeButton={false}` it gives a non-button element `role="button"`, a `tabIndex` and Enter and Space activation, and in development it warns when `nativeButton` doesn't match the rendered element.

## Props

In MUI's layout, as MUI's IconButton takes its icon as `children`. Every prop the component declares gets this description as its JSDoc; the inherited rows keep Base UI's. Slots come last.

The button is named by a required `label: string` prop, rendered as text inside the button through the `VisuallyHidden` shared part, rather than by the caller's `aria-label`. The type then makes the name impossible to forget, which Button's spec promises ("so it gets its required label"); the contract composes `VisuallyHidden` for a word the eye gets from an icon; and a page translator rewrites text inside the button, where it leaves an `aria-label` in the other language. A caller's `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` still wins, through `{...rest}`.

IconButton takes a `size` of `'medium' | 'large'`, default `'medium'`, that keeps the `size.control` square and sets only the icon's step: `icon.size.400` for `medium`, `icon.size.450` for `large`. [Icons](../foundations/icons.md#sizes) gives `icon.size.450` to "top bar buttons" (`monitor` and `info`, drawn on the 18 px grid), which are icon buttons, and an icon drawn on one grid must not be scaled to another; no token gives an icon button a second box size.

IconButton leaves out MUI IconButton's `edge` and `loading`. No source asks for either: the screens place their buttons with layout gaps, and no Perron component shows a loading indicator yet. Each can join later as a new optional prop, which the contract's [Change](README.md#change) rule allows.

| Name                        | Type                   | Default     | Base UI prop         | Description                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------- | ----------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `label`                     | `string`               | none        | none                 | The words that name the action, in sentence case, such as "Zoom in". Required: the icon is hidden from screen readers, so these words are the button's name. Never seen, read by screen readers. |
| `color`                     | `'neutral' \| 'brand'` | `'neutral'` | none                 | The intent: `neutral` is quiet ink, for every action but the main one; `brand` is the brand yellow, for the one main action of a screen.                                                         |
| `size`                      | `'medium' \| 'large'`  | `'medium'`  | none                 | The icon's step in the `size.control` square: `medium` is `icon.size.400`, for icons drawn on the 16 px grid; `large` is `icon.size.450`, for the top bar's icons drawn on the 18 px grid.       |
| `disabled`                  | `boolean`              | `false`     | `disabled`           | Whether the button ignores the pointer and the keys. A disabled button leaves the tab order unless `focusableWhenDisabled` is set.                                                               |
| `focusableWhenDisabled`     | `boolean`              | `false`     | inherited            | Whether the button should be focusable when disabled.                                                                                                                                            |
| `nativeButton`              | `boolean`              | `true`      | inherited            | Whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `false` if the rendered element is not a button (for example, `<div>`).                |
| `render`                    | Base UI's `render`     | none        | inherited            | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.        |
| `children`                  | `ReactNode`            | none        | none                 | The icon, such as an SVG from `packages/perron/icons/` with the `perron-icon` class. Hidden from screen readers: `label` names the button.                                                       |
| `className`, `style`, `ref` | React's                | none        | `className`, `style` | Reach the root. `className` is merged after `pn-IconButton`.                                                                                                                                     |

No `slotProps`: IconButton has one Base UI part, `Button`, which is the root, and the root takes the component's own props. The icon span and the label's `VisuallyHidden` are not Base UI parts. No label-override props: `label` is the caller's word, not an owned string.

## Tokens

One row per part, state and property. States are the contract's design states; the deferred design's `State` values map as Button's do: `default` is rest, `hover` is `:hover` inside `@media (hover: hover)`, `focus` is `:focus-visible`, `disabled` is `[data-disabled]`; pressed, which the design doesn't draw, is `:active`. Every `color` row sets the root's `color`, which the icon takes through `currentColor`.

IconButton has no `variant` prop and one look per colour, as Toolbar's icon-only buttons have: `neutral` quiet (transparent at rest in `color.text.primary`, `color.surface.hover` on hover and press), `brand` a solid brand button (`color.surface.brand` with a `color.border.brand` edge and `color.text.on-color.dark`, `color.surface.brand-hover` on hover and press). Icon buttons sit on panels, sheets and the top bar's glass, which already mark where they are; the brand is calm, with ink and neutral surfaces around the map; MUI's IconButton has no `variant` either; and a toolbar of icon buttons then matches the IconButtons beside it.

IconButton leaves out a toggled ("pressed") state, `aria-pressed` and the `color.surface.inverse` fill whose description names "pressed icon buttons", leaving an icon that turns something on and off to a component on Base UI's `Toggle`. IconButton's one Base UI part is `Button`, which keeps no pressed state; [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#rules) wants a toggle's state said in words as well as looks, which a label-only button can't show; and FilterChip and HighlightChip, on `Toggle`, are the roadmap's toggles.

Every colour and size:

| Part        | State | Property                    | Token                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------- | ----- | --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`      | rest  | `width`, `height`           | `size.control`                                                                                                                            |
| `root`      | rest  | `padding`                   | 0                                                                                                                                         |
| `root`      | rest  | `border-radius`             | `radius.md`                                                                                                                               |
| `root`      | rest  | `border-width`              | `border.width.025`                                                                                                                        |
| `root`      | rest  | `--perron-icon-size`        | `icon.size.400` when `size` is `medium`, `icon.size.450` when `large`, inherited by the icon                                              |
| `root`      | focus | `outline`, `outline-offset` | `focus.width` in `color.border.focus`, `focus.offset` (drawn by `perron.css`)                                                             |
| `focusRing` | focus | ring corner radius          | `radius.lg`, as Button's: the outline follows the root's `radius.md` out by `focus.offset` plus `focus.width`, and the CSS sets no radius |

`neutral`:

| Part   | State    | Property           | Token                 |
| ------ | -------- | ------------------ | --------------------- |
| `root` | rest     | `background-color` | `transparent`         |
| `root` | rest     | `border-color`     | `transparent`         |
| `root` | rest     | `color`            | `color.text.primary`  |
| `root` | hover    | `background-color` | `color.surface.hover` |
| `root` | pressed  | `background-color` | `color.surface.hover` |
| `root` | disabled | `background-color` | `transparent`         |
| `root` | disabled | `color`            | `color.text.tertiary` |

`brand`:

| Part   | State    | Property           | Token                       |
| ------ | -------- | ------------------ | --------------------------- |
| `root` | rest     | `background-color` | `color.surface.brand`       |
| `root` | rest     | `border-color`     | `color.border.brand`        |
| `root` | rest     | `color`            | `color.text.on-color.dark`  |
| `root` | hover    | `background-color` | `color.surface.brand-hover` |
| `root` | pressed  | `background-color` | `color.surface.brand-hover` |
| `root` | disabled | `background-color` | `color.surface.inset`       |
| `root` | disabled | `border-color`     | `transparent`               |
| `root` | disabled | `color`            | `color.text.tertiary`       |

A disabled brand icon button looks like Button's disabled solid one, `color.surface.inset` with `color.text.tertiary` and no edge: disabled is a colour, and a yellow that can't be pressed shouldn't still mark the main action.

Pressed takes the hover row's tokens, in a rule outside `@media (hover: hover)` so a press on a touch screen shows, as on Button: no token is made for a pressed fill.

Highlighted, open, selected and invalid don't apply: Base UI's `Button` produces only `data-disabled`, a button takes focus rather than `data-highlighted`, a popup trigger given through `render` keeps the button's look while its popup is open, and an icon button holds no choice or value.

## Keyboard and ARIA

From the Base UI reference for `Button` and the installed `useButton`, as on Button. "From" says who does it.

| Key                | Does                                                                                            | From                                           |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`, `Shift+Tab` | Moves focus to the button and away; a disabled button is skipped unless `focusableWhenDisabled` | The browser, and Base UI                       |
| `Enter`            | Activates the button: fires `onClick`, or submits the form with `type="submit"`                 | The browser; Base UI for a non-button `render` |
| `Space`            | Activates the button on release                                                                 | The browser; Base UI for a non-button `render` |

| Element | Role                                                                                    | Accessible name from                                                                                              | States announced                                                                 |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`  | `button`, native; `role="button"` from Base UI when `render` gives a non-button element | Its text content: the `label` in the `VisuallyHidden` span; `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` from the caller win | Disabled: the native `disabled`, or `aria-disabled` with `focusableWhenDisabled` |
| `icon`  | none: `aria-hidden="true"`                                                              | none                                                                                                              | none                                                                             |
| `label` | none: text inside the button                                                            | none: it is the name                                                                                              | none                                                                             |

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the icon is `aria-hidden` and `label` says in words what it shows, as [Icons](../foundations/icons.md#style) asks of an icon alone; `color` carries emphasis, not meaning; disabled is announced by the native attribute or `aria-disabled`.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: none here; a button is neither.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: none here; IconButton owns no strings, and `label` is the caller's.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `children` renders a string, an element and a list alike, centred in the square, in both colours and both sizes, and the icon span clips a string wider than the square so it stays inside; `label` is a `string`.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; IconButton keeps no hidden copy and collapses nothing. The `VisuallyHidden` label is the name, not a copy.
- [ ] Native semantics first: a native `<button>` from Base UI's `Button`, named by its own text; with `render` and `nativeButton={false}`, Base UI's `role="button"`. No ARIA of its own.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: the button is one tab stop in document order, and opens nothing of its own to return from.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: every IconButton is `size.control` (34 px) square, in both sizes.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; IconButton has no loop and no transition.

## Owned strings

No owned strings: every word comes from the caller, as `label`.

## Component rules

Rules for this component alone, numbered so the build and the review can cite them.

- **CR-1.** Base UI's `Button` already renders the native `<button type="button">`, activates on Enter and Space, sets `disabled` and `data-disabled`, and blocks the click of a disabled button, so the component rebuilds none of it and passes `disabled` straight to it.
- **CR-2.** The root always carries `data-color` and `data-size`, defaults included; the CSS selects on them, one class then attributes: `.pn-IconButton[data-color='brand']`, `.pn-IconButton[data-size='large']`.
- **CR-3.** The root is a `size.control` square in both sizes, with no padding, and centres the icon (`display: inline-flex`, `align-items` and `justify-content` `center`, `flex: none` so a flex row never squeezes it). The icon span is at most the square and clips what overflows it, so a long string stays inside the square and the root's ring and label are untouched. `size` changes only the icon's step.
- **CR-4.** The states keep the geometry: hover, pressed, focus and disabled change colours only, never the size, border width or radius. Both colours draw a `border.width.025` border, `transparent` on `neutral` and on a disabled `brand`, so the two share one box and Windows' forced colours draw an edge round every icon button.
- **CR-5.** Hover is read inside `@media (hover: hover)`; pressed (`:active`) takes the hover tokens in a rule outside it, so a touch press shows. Neither applies to a disabled button: both rules exclude `[data-disabled]`, since a native disabled button still matches `:hover`, and one with `focusableWhenDisabled` still matches `:active`.
- **CR-6.** Focus uses the ring `perron.css` draws on `:focus-visible`; the component draws no ring of its own and never removes the outline. The focus state otherwise looks like rest.
- **CR-7.** The colour is set on the root's `color`; the icon takes it through `currentColor`. No rule sets a colour on the icon.
- **CR-8.** The icon span is `aria-hidden="true"`, and the root sets `--perron-icon-size`, which the icon inherits: `icon.size.400` for `medium`, `icon.size.450` for `large`, on `.pn-IconButton` and `.pn-IconButton[data-size='large']` with no descendant selector, so an icon from `packages/perron/icons/` renders at the step its grid was drawn for.
- **CR-9.** The label is the caller's `label` inside the `VisuallyHidden` shared part, after the icon span, rendered on every button: the button is named by its own text, the component sets no `aria-label` and no `title`, and `label` is required in `IconButtonProps`.
- **CR-10.** A `brand` icon button keeps its `color.border.brand` edge at rest, on hover and pressed: the light-theme yellow fill reaches only 2.1:1 on the surfaces, and the edge carries the 3:1 ([Semantic colours](../foundations/semantic-colours.md#brand)).
- **CR-11.** Changes of state are immediate: no `duration.*` token fits a button's state change, so the CSS has no transition.
- **CR-12.** `{...rest}` reaches the root before the component's own attributes, and `label`, `color`, `size` and `children` are taken out of `rest` first, so none reaches the DOM as an attribute.
- **CR-13.** In forced colours, a disabled icon button draws its edge and its icon in `GrayText`, inside `@media (forced-colors: active)`, as Button does.
- **CR-14.** IconButton keeps no toggled state: it sets no `aria-pressed`, and no rule reads one.

## Stories

The deferred design's variant properties, in this order: `color` (`neutral`, `brand`), `size` (`medium`, `large`) and `State` (`default`, `hover`, `focus`, `disabled`). Each story is named by its variant name (`penpot/README.md`, "Conventions"). A `medium` story renders `packages/perron/icons/`'s `plus` with the label "Zoom in"; a `large` one renders `info`, drawn on the 18 px grid, with the label "Show help". A `Disabled` story sets `disabled`. The hover and focus stories render at rest: the visual check drives the state itself, and their `play` tests check it.

| Story                   | Shows                     | `play` test                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `NeutralMediumDefault`  | neutral, medium, at rest  | The button's accessible name is "Zoom in" and its icon span is `aria-hidden`; Tab focuses it, Enter and Space each fire `onClick` once, Shift+Tab returns focus |
| `NeutralMediumHover`    | neutral, medium, hover    | Hovering lays `color.surface.hover` over the transparent fill                                                                                                   |
| `NeutralMediumFocus`    | neutral, medium, focus    | Tab gives the root `:focus-visible` and the ring                                                                                                                |
| `NeutralMediumDisabled` | neutral, medium, disabled | The button has `disabled` and `data-disabled`, Tab skips it, and a click fires no `onClick`                                                                     |
| `NeutralLargeDefault`   | neutral, large, at rest   | The root is `size.control` square, as in `medium`, and the icon renders at `icon.size.450`                                                                      |
| `NeutralLargeHover`     | neutral, large, hover     | none                                                                                                                                                            |
| `NeutralLargeFocus`     | neutral, large, focus     | none                                                                                                                                                            |
| `NeutralLargeDisabled`  | neutral, large, disabled  | none                                                                                                                                                            |
| `BrandMediumDefault`    | brand, medium, at rest    | none                                                                                                                                                            |
| `BrandMediumHover`      | brand, medium, hover      | Hovering sets the `color.surface.brand-hover` fill and keeps the `color.border.brand` edge                                                                      |
| `BrandMediumFocus`      | brand, medium, focus      | none                                                                                                                                                            |
| `BrandMediumDisabled`   | brand, medium, disabled   | The disabled brand button has the `color.surface.inset` fill and a transparent edge                                                                             |
| `BrandLargeDefault`     | brand, large, at rest     | none                                                                                                                                                            |
| `BrandLargeHover`       | brand, large, hover       | none                                                                                                                                                            |
| `BrandLargeFocus`       | brand, large, focus       | none                                                                                                                                                            |
| `BrandLargeDisabled`    | brand, large, disabled    | none                                                                                                                                                            |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                                                         | Don't                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Give `label` the action in sentence case, as a verb and what it acts on: "Zoom in", "Centre the map"                                                       | Name the icon rather than the action ("Plus", "Magnifier"), or write Title Case or an exclamation mark ([Content design](../content-design.md)) |
| Use IconButton only where the icon is one people know at a glance, such as zoom, locate, close or search, and use [Button](button.md) with words otherwise | Put an icon whose meaning has to be guessed in an IconButton: the label reaches only screen readers, and the eye gets the icon alone            |
| Give `size="large"` to an icon drawn on the 18 px grid (`monitor`, `info`), and keep the default `medium` for the 16 px ones                               | Set `--perron-icon-size` or a width on the icon yourself, or give a 16 px icon `large`: an icon drawn on one grid blurs when scaled to another  |
| Give one action per screen `color="brand"`, for its main action                                                                                            | Use `brand` for emphasis, or set two brand actions on one screen                                                                                |
| Set icon buttons on a panel, a sheet or the top bar's glass, which mark where they sit                                                                     | Float a `neutral` icon button straight over the map: its transparent fill disappears on the land and water                                      |
| Put each action of a [Toolbar](toolbar.md) in a `ToolbarButton`, so the arrow keys reach it                                                                | Put an IconButton inside a Toolbar: it falls out of the arrow-key order and adds a tab stop                                                     |
| Use a toggle component, such as FilterChip, for an icon that turns something on and off                                                                    | Set `aria-pressed` on an IconButton and restyle it: IconButton keeps no pressed state, and a toggle says its state in words                     |
| Set `disabled` when the action can't run, with `focusableWhenDisabled` so the button can still be reached and its name heard                               | Restyle a disabled icon button with `opacity`: disabled is `color.text.tertiary`, a colour                                                      |

title: LinkButton
markdown:
# LinkButton

A link that looks like a [Button](button.md): it takes the reader to another page or place, such as "Back to the map" or "Open in Rejseplanen", where a Button runs an action on the screen it sits on.

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): there is no read-back, code map or export, and this spec decides what the drawing would, from the contract, the foundations, the tokens, the Base UI reference and the [Button](button.md) spec, the one entry in its `dependsOn`. Base UI's Button guide settles the shape: Base UI's `Button` "enforces button semantics" (`role="button"`, Space activation) and "should not be used for links", and "if a link needs to look like a button visually, style the `<a>` element directly with CSS". So LinkButton is a native `<a href>` with Button's look, not a Button with `render={<a />}`.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/LinkButton`. Family: none (the contract's [Families](README.md#families) give buttons only their text, `typography.label`, and LinkButton wears Button's treatment). Shared parts: none.

LinkButton has no Base UI part: the registry gives it none, and Base UI's only candidate, `Button`, would give the link a button's role. Its root renders through Base UI's `useRender` hook (`@base-ui/react/use-render`), which gives it the `render` prop, as Delay's does, and its inner parts are plain elements. The layers are the ones the drawing will name, Button's own.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                                | Base UI part                                      | Class                     | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | The native `<a href>`: an inline flex row, centred, that holds the start icon, the label and the end icon in reading order                | none: an `<a>` rendered by `useRender`            | `pn-LinkButton`           | none            |
| `label`             | A `<span>` that holds the caller's `children`                                                                                             | none: a plain `<span>`, no behaviour to borrow    | `pn-LinkButton-label`     | none            |
| `startIcon`         | A `<span>`, `aria-hidden`, that holds the caller's `startIcon` before the label; only rendered when `startIcon` is given                  | none: a plain `<span>`                            | `pn-LinkButton-startIcon` | none            |
| `endIcon`           | A `<span>`, `aria-hidden`, that holds the caller's `endIcon` after the label; only rendered when `endIcon` is given                       | none: a plain `<span>`                            | `pn-LinkButton-endIcon`   | none            |
| `focusRing`         | The keyboard focus ring: the `:focus-visible` outline `perron.css` draws on the root, not an element; the code map will land it on `root` | none: the browser's `:focus-visible` on the `<a>` | none                      | none            |

LinkButton has its own CSS, `pn-LinkButton`, that sets Button's tokens row for row (see Tokens), rather than reusing Button's classes or composing Perron's `Button`: the contract names each component's classes after it, composing `Button` would bring Base UI's `role="button"`, and ToolbarButton already set the precedent of its own CSS over Button's tokens. A story holds the two to each other (`MatchesButton`).

## Base UI parts

LinkButton imports no Base UI component. It uses two Base UI utilities, at the version pinned in `package.json` (1.9.0 installed): `useRender` (`@base-ui/react/use-render`) for the root and `mergeProps` (`@base-ui/react/merge-props`) to merge the caller's props with its own.

| Base UI part                     | Renders                              | Perron sets                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Passed through                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `useRender` (a hook, not a part) | `<a>`, or the element `render` gives | `defaultTagName: 'a'`, `className` (`pn-LinkButton`, then the caller's), `href` from `href`, `data-variant` and `data-size` (defaults included), `data-full-width` when `fullWidth`, the icon and label spans | `render`, `ref`, `className`, `style`, `target`, `rel`, `download`, `hrefLang`, `aria-current`, `onClick` and every other prop of a native `<a>`, through `mergeProps` |

Base UI already does: swapping the root element for the one `render` gives (a router's link component, for one), keeping the class, the data attributes and the children; merging the caller's `ref` with the element's; and merging event handlers, `className` and `style` through `mergeProps`. Everything a link does, the browser does: Enter follows it, a middle click or a modifier opens it in a new tab or window, the context menu offers to copy it, and assistive technology lists it among the page's links.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop here gets this description as its JSDoc. LinkButton has no `slotProps`, because the contract keys `slotProps` by inner Base UI part and LinkButton has none; a caller restyles it through `className` on the root. It owns no strings, so it has no label-override props. The `<a>` element's other attributes (`target`, `rel`, `download`, `aria-current`) reach the root and get no row, as the contract's [Props](README.md#props) says.

LinkButton offers Button's `variant` (`'solid' | 'outline'`, default `'solid'`), `size` (`'small' | 'medium'`, default `'medium'`), `fullWidth`, `startIcon` and `endIcon`, with Button's meanings and tokens, so a link and a button side by side look alike.

LinkButton has no `color` prop and is always ink (Button's `neutral`): the contract's [Intents](README.md#intents) say `brand` "is never a link" and offer it to Button, IconButton and a Toolbar's buttons only, and [Semantic colours](../foundations/semantic-colours.md#brand) say links have their own colours. A `color` prop can join later, as a wider union, without a break.

LinkButton has no `disabled` prop: an `<a>` has no `disabled` attribute, an `<a>` without `href` has no role for `aria-disabled` to sit on, and a link that goes nowhere shouldn't be shown; a caller who needs a disabled look renders a disabled Button.

LinkButton declares `href` itself, optional, with its own JSDoc, so the docs page shows it, though the contract leaves the element's attributes without a row: it is the one attribute every LinkButton needs, and it is optional only because a `render` such as a router's link can bring its own (`to`).

| Name                 | Type                     | Default    | Base UI prop         | Description                                                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------------- | ------------------------ | ---------- | -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `href`               | `string`                 | none       | none                 | Where the link goes: a URL or a path. Give it on every LinkButton, unless `render` gives a router's link that brings its own destination.                                                 |
| `variant`            | `'solid' \| 'outline'`   | `'solid'`  | none                 | How much the link stands out: `solid` is filled, for the main place a panel leads to; `outline` is an edge only, for the links and actions beside it.                                     |
| `size`               | `'small' \| 'medium'`    | `'medium'` | none                 | The link's height: `medium` is `size.button`, `small` is `size.button-sm`, for dense rows and panels.                                                                                     |
| `fullWidth`          | `boolean`                | `false`    | none                 | Whether the link fills the width of its container, such as a bottom sheet's main link. Sets `data-full-width`.                                                                            |
| `startIcon`          | `ReactNode`              | none       | none                 | An icon before the label, in reading order, so it moves to the right in right-to-left text. Hidden from screen readers: the label names the link.                                         |
| `endIcon`            | `ReactNode`              | none       | none                 | An icon after the label, in reading order. Hidden from screen readers: the label names the link.                                                                                          |
| `render`             | Base UI's `render`       |            | inherited            | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `children`           | `ReactNode`              | none       | none                 | The label: the words that name where the link goes, in sentence case. Required in practice: a link with no words has no name.                                                             |
| `className`, `style` | React's                  | none       | through `mergeProps` | Reach the root; `className` is merged after `pn-LinkButton`.                                                                                                                              |
| `ref`                | `Ref<HTMLAnchorElement>` | none       | `useRender`'s `ref`  | Reaches the root element.                                                                                                                                                                 |

`render` is Base UI's, inherited as it is. With none, LinkButton renders an `<a>` (CR-1); `render` swaps it, such as for a router's link component, keeping the class, the data attributes and the children, and the element it gives must render an `<a>` too.

## Tokens

One row per part, state and property, Button's own for the variants LinkButton offers ([Button](button.md#tokens)). States are the contract's design states: rest is no selector, hover is `:hover` inside `@media (hover: hover)`, focus is `:focus-visible`, pressed is `:active`. A link has no disabled, open, selected or invalid state, and `:visited` is not a design state, so a visited LinkButton looks as it did before. Every `color` row sets the root's `color`, which the label and both icons take, since icons draw in `currentColor`.

All variants:

| Part                   | State | Property                    | Token                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------------- | ----- | --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`, medium         | rest  | `height`                    | `size.button`                                                                                                                    |
| `root`, medium         | rest  | `padding-inline`            | `space.400`                                                                                                                      |
| `root`, medium         | rest  | `gap`                       | `space.200`                                                                                                                      |
| `root`, small          | rest  | `height`                    | `size.button-sm`                                                                                                                 |
| `root`, small          | rest  | `padding-inline`            | `space.300`                                                                                                                      |
| `root`, small          | rest  | `gap`                       | `space.150`                                                                                                                      |
| `root`                 | rest  | `border-radius`             | `radius.md`                                                                                                                      |
| `root`                 | rest  | `border-width`              | `border.width.025`                                                                                                               |
| `root`                 | rest  | `text-decoration`           | none: the keyword `none`, since the shape marks the link (CR-6)                                                                  |
| `label`                | rest  | `font`, `letter-spacing`    | `typography.label`, with its tracking twin                                                                                       |
| `startIcon`, `endIcon` | rest  | `--perron-icon-size`        | `icon.size.400`                                                                                                                  |
| `root`                 | focus | `outline`, `outline-offset` | `focus.width` in `color.border.focus`, `focus.offset` (drawn by `perron.css`)                                                    |
| `focusRing`            | focus | ring corner radius          | `radius.lg`, as Button's: the outline follows the root's `radius.md` out by `focus.offset` plus `focus.width`, no CSS of its own |

`solid`:

| Part   | State   | Property           | Token                         |
| ------ | ------- | ------------------ | ----------------------------- |
| `root` | rest    | `background-color` | `color.surface.inverse`       |
| `root` | rest    | `border-color`     | `transparent`                 |
| `root` | rest    | `color`            | `color.text.inverse`          |
| `root` | hover   | `background-color` | `color.surface.inverse-hover` |
| `root` | pressed | `background-color` | `color.surface.inverse-hover` |

`outline`:

| Part   | State   | Property           | Token                  |
| ------ | ------- | ------------------ | ---------------------- |
| `root` | rest    | `background-color` | `transparent`          |
| `root` | rest    | `border-color`     | `color.border.control` |
| `root` | rest    | `color`            | `color.text.primary`   |
| `root` | hover   | `background-color` | `color.surface.hover`  |
| `root` | pressed | `background-color` | `color.surface.hover`  |

Pressed takes the hover row's tokens, in a rule outside `@media (hover: hover)` so a touch press shows, as Button's CR-13 does: no token is made for a pressed fill.

## Keyboard and ARIA

From the browser's native link and Base UI's `useRender`, which adds no behaviour. "From" says who does it.

| Key                | Does                                                                                 | From        |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------- |
| `Tab`, `Shift+Tab` | Moves focus to the link and away                                                     | The browser |
| `Enter`            | Follows the link: fires `onClick`, then goes to `href` unless the click is prevented | The browser |
| `Space`            | Nothing: Space scrolls the page, as on every link, and never follows it (CR-4)       | The browser |

| Element                | Role                            | Accessible name from                                                                            | States announced                                                |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`                 | `link`, native, from `<a href>` | Its text content: the label's `children`; `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` from the caller win | Visited, by the browser; `aria-current` when the caller sets it |
| `startIcon`, `endIcon` | none: `aria-hidden="true"`      | none                                                                                            | none                                                            |

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the label is text the link is named by; the icons are `aria-hidden`, since an icon beside a word adds nothing the word doesn't say ([Icons](../foundations/icons.md#style)); `variant` carries emphasis, not meaning; and the role says "link" where the shape says "button", so the label names where it goes (see Do and don't).
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: none here; a link is neither.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: none here; LinkButton owns no strings.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `children`, `startIcon` and `endIcon` render a string, an element and a list alike, in every `variant` and `size`.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; LinkButton keeps no hidden copy and collapses nothing.
- [ ] Native semantics first: a native `<a href>`, never `role="button"` and never Base UI's `Button` (CR-1); a `render` element renders an `<a>` too.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: the link is one tab stop in document order, and opens nothing of its own to return from.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: the smallest target is a small LinkButton, `size.button-sm` (30 px) tall, and at least that wide with its `space.300` padding on each side and a word between.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; LinkButton has no loop and no transition.

## Owned strings

No owned strings: every word comes from the caller, as `children`.

LinkButton announces nothing of its own when `target="_blank"` opens a new tab, and owns no "Opens in a new tab" string: a link that leaves Mylder names its destination in its label ("Open in Rejseplanen"), and Mylder's own links open in the same tab.

## Component rules

Rules for this component alone, numbered so the build and the review can cite them.

- **CR-1.** The root is a native `<a>` through `useRender` with `defaultTagName: 'a'`, never Base UI's `Button` or Perron's `Button` with `render={<a />}`: Base UI's `Button` gives a non-button element `role="button"` and Space activation, which tell a screen reader a link is a button.
- **CR-2.** The root always carries `data-variant` and `data-size`, defaults included, and `data-full-width` when `fullWidth`; the CSS selects on them, one class then attributes: `.pn-LinkButton[data-variant='outline'][data-size='small']`.
- **CR-3.** LinkButton's CSS sets, for each `variant` and `size`, the tokens Button's sets for the same `variant` and `size` in its `neutral` colour (see Tokens), so a LinkButton and a Button side by side share their height, padding, gap, radius, border, font and colours in every state. A change to Button's tokens changes LinkButton's in the same PR.
- **CR-4.** LinkButton adds no keyboard handling: Enter follows the link through the browser, Space does nothing to it, and modifier clicks open it in a new tab or window, as on every link.
- **CR-5.** The states keep the link's geometry: hover, pressed and focus change colours only, never the height, padding, gap, border width or radius, so nothing moves when the state changes. Hover is read inside `@media (hover: hover)`; pressed (`:active`) takes the hover row's tokens outside it.
- **CR-6.** The root resets the browser's link styles: `text-decoration: none` in every state, and its `color` from the tokens in every state, `:visited` included, so a visited LinkButton looks as it did before. Its shape marks it as something to press, as Button's does.
- **CR-7.** Focus uses the ring `perron.css` draws on `:focus-visible`; the component draws no ring of its own and never removes the outline.
- **CR-8.** The colour is set on the root's `color`; the label and the icons take it, the icons through `currentColor`. No rule sets a colour on an icon.
- **CR-9.** The icon spans are `aria-hidden="true"`, rendered only when their prop renders something (`false`, `true`, `null`, `undefined` and `''` leave no span, as in Button), and set `--perron-icon-size` to `icon.size.400` in both sizes.
- **CR-10.** Every variant draws a `border.width.025` border, `transparent` on a solid link, so both looks share one box and Windows' forced colours draw an edge round every LinkButton, as Button's CR-11 does.
- **CR-11.** The label stays on one line (`white-space: nowrap`), the link growing with it, rather than wrapping inside the fixed `size.button` height, as Button's CR-12 does.
- **CR-12.** Changes of state are immediate: no `duration.*` token fits the change, so the CSS has no transition.
- **CR-13.** The caller's props reach the root through `mergeProps`, the component's own last, so the component's class, data attributes and children win, and `variant`, `size`, `fullWidth`, `startIcon` and `endIcon` are taken out first, so none reaches the DOM. `className` is merged after `pn-LinkButton`.
- **CR-14.** LinkButton takes no `color` and no `disabled`: it is always ink, Button's `neutral`, and has no disabled state. Its props type is the `<a>` element's with React's non-standard `color` attribute omitted, so `color="brand"` is a type error rather than an attribute on the DOM; the `<a>` element's type already has no `disabled`.
- **CR-15.** `href` is declared in LinkButton's own props, optional, with its Props row's description as its JSDoc, and reaches the root's `<a>` as its `href`.

## Stories

The deferred design's variant properties, in this order: `variant` (`solid`, `outline`), `size` (`medium`, `small`) and `State` (`default`, `hover`, `focus`). Each story is named by its variant name (`penpot/README.md`, "Conventions"), renders the label "Back to the map" with an `href`, and its link's click is prevented in the story so a `play` test never leaves the page. The hover and focus stories render at rest: the visual check drives the state itself, and their `play` tests check it. Button's `disabled` State has no LinkButton twin, since LinkButton has no disabled state.

| Story                  | Shows                                                                                               | `play` test                                                                                                                                         |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SolidMediumDefault`   | solid, medium, at rest                                                                              | The root is a `link` named "Back to the map" with its `href`; Tab focuses it, Enter fires `onClick` once, Space fires none, Shift+Tab returns focus |
| `SolidMediumHover`     | solid, medium, hover                                                                                | Hovering sets the `color.surface.inverse-hover` fill                                                                                                |
| `SolidMediumFocus`     | solid, medium, focus                                                                                | Tab gives the root `:focus-visible` and the ring                                                                                                    |
| `SolidSmallDefault`    | solid, small, at rest                                                                               | none                                                                                                                                                |
| `SolidSmallHover`      | solid, small, hover                                                                                 | none                                                                                                                                                |
| `SolidSmallFocus`      | solid, small, focus                                                                                 | none                                                                                                                                                |
| `OutlineMediumDefault` | outline, medium, at rest                                                                            | none                                                                                                                                                |
| `OutlineMediumHover`   | outline, medium, hover                                                                              | Hovering lays `color.surface.hover` over the transparent fill                                                                                       |
| `OutlineMediumFocus`   | outline, medium, focus                                                                              | none                                                                                                                                                |
| `OutlineSmallDefault`  | outline, small, at rest                                                                             | none                                                                                                                                                |
| `OutlineSmallHover`    | outline, small, hover                                                                               | none                                                                                                                                                |
| `OutlineSmallFocus`    | outline, small, focus                                                                               | none                                                                                                                                                |
| `WithIcons`            | solid, medium, at rest, with a `startIcon` and an `endIcon` from `packages/perron/icons/`           | The icon spans are `aria-hidden`, and the link's accessible name is the label alone                                                                 |
| `FullWidth`            | outline, medium, at rest, `fullWidth` in a narrow container                                         | The root carries `data-full-width` and is as wide as its container                                                                                  |
| `RenderedLink`         | solid, medium, at rest, with `render` giving a router-style link component that renders an `<a>`    | The root is still one `link` with `pn-LinkButton`, `data-variant` and `data-size`, and the `ref` reaches it                                         |
| `MatchesButton`        | A LinkButton beside a Button with the same label, in each `variant` and `size`, Button in `neutral` | Each pair's computed height, padding, border, radius, font, background and colour are equal (CR-3), and `:visited` changes none of the LinkButton's |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                            | Don't                                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Use LinkButton when pressing it goes somewhere: another page, another place in the app, another site                          | Use LinkButton to run an action, such as showing a line or closing a panel, with an `onClick` that prevents the link: that is a Button                 |
| Use Button for an action and LinkButton for navigation, even when they sit side by side and look alike                        | Render a link through Button's `render={<a href="/map" />}`: Base UI gives it `role="button"`, and a screen reader hears a button that navigates       |
| Name where the link goes, in sentence case: "Back to the map", "Open in Rejseplanen"                                          | Write "Click here", "Read more", Title Case or an exclamation mark ([Content design](../content-design.md)): the role already says it is a link        |
| Give a router's link through `render`, such as `render={<Link to="/map" />}`, so the app's navigation runs and the look stays | Wrap a LinkButton in a router link, or a router link in a LinkButton: two nested `<a>` elements are invalid and make two tab stops                     |
| Use a plain `<a>` inside a sentence, where a link is part of the text                                                         | Put a LinkButton in running text: its height and padding break the line                                                                                |
| Keep LinkButton in ink; give the screen's one main action to a `brand` Button                                                 | Restyle a LinkButton in the brand yellow: brand is never a link ([Intents](README.md#intents))                                                         |
| Leave a link out, or show a disabled Button, when there is nowhere to go yet                                                  | Render a LinkButton without `href` or `render`, or fake a disabled one with `opacity`: an `<a>` with no `href` is not a link, and disabled is a colour |
| Use IconButton for a control with an icon and no words                                                                        | Pass only a `startIcon` and no `children`: the icon is `aria-hidden`, so the link has no name                                                          |

title: Toolbar
markdown:
# Toolbar

A bar of actions that is one tab stop, moved through with the arrow keys, such as the map's zoom and locate controls or a glass group in the top bar.

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): there is no read-back, code map or export, and this spec decides what the drawing would, from the contract, the foundations, the tokens and the Base UI reference. The extracted prototype component is not in any branch this run can reach.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/Toolbar`. Family: none (the contract's [Families](README.md#families) have no bar of actions; the root borrows the Popups' glass, see Tokens). Shared parts: none (an icon-only button is named by the caller's `aria-label`, not by `VisuallyHidden`).

The `Toolbar` folder holds four components, `Toolbar`, `ToolbarButton`, `ToolbarGroup` and `ToolbarSeparator`, each exported with its props type from `Toolbar.tsx`, as an exception to the contract's "one component per folder": Toolbar's Base UI parts share one context (`Toolbar.Button`, `Toolbar.Group` and `Toolbar.Separator` read `Toolbar.Root`'s), so they can't be built or shown apart. The `props` and `api-compatibility` checks read only `ToolbarProps`, so the review holds the other three to the contract.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                                  | Base UI part                         | Class                        | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | `Toolbar`: the bar, a flex row (or column when vertical) on glass, that holds the caller's buttons, groups and separators                   | `Toolbar.Root`                       | `pn-Toolbar`                 | none            |
| `button`            | `ToolbarButton`: the native `<button>` of one action, a flex row, centred, that holds the start icon, the label and the end icon            | `Toolbar.Button`                     | `pn-ToolbarButton`           | none            |
| `label`             | A `<span>` in `ToolbarButton` that holds the caller's `children`; only rendered when `children` is given                                    | none: a span inside `Toolbar.Button` | `pn-ToolbarButton-label`     | none            |
| `startIcon`         | A `<span>`, `aria-hidden`, in `ToolbarButton` that holds the caller's `startIcon` before the label; only rendered when `startIcon` is given | none: a span inside `Toolbar.Button` | `pn-ToolbarButton-startIcon` | none            |
| `endIcon`           | A `<span>`, `aria-hidden`, in `ToolbarButton` that holds the caller's `endIcon` after the label; only rendered when `endIcon` is given      | none: a span inside `Toolbar.Button` | `pn-ToolbarButton-endIcon`   | none            |
| `group`             | `ToolbarGroup`: a flex row (or column) of related buttons, with no look of its own                                                          | `Toolbar.Group`                      | `pn-ToolbarGroup`            | none            |
| `separator`         | `ToolbarSeparator`: a hairline between buttons or groups, across the bar                                                                    | `Toolbar.Separator`                  | `pn-ToolbarSeparator`        | none            |
| `focusRing`         | The keyboard focus ring on a button: the `:focus-visible` outline `perron.css` draws on `button`, not an element                            | `Toolbar.Button`                     | none                         | none            |

Base UI's `Toolbar.Link` and `Toolbar.Input` are not offered: the registry doesn't name them, a link among buttons reads as an action, and the Base UI guidance keeps inputs to one, last, since the arrow keys both move the caret and leave the field.

## Base UI parts

Imported from `@base-ui/react/toolbar`, at the version pinned in `package.json` (1.9.0 installed).

| Base UI part        | Renders                                                                                                                                     | Perron sets                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Passed through                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Toolbar.Root`      | `<div role="toolbar" aria-orientation>`, with `data-orientation` and, when disabled, `data-disabled`                                        | `className` (`pn-Toolbar`, then the caller's), `ref`, `orientation` and `disabled` from `Toolbar`'s props                                                                                                        | `loopFocus`, `render`, `style`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` and every other prop of a `<div>`, through `{...rest}`                               |
| `Toolbar.Button`    | `<button type="button">`, with `data-orientation`, `data-disabled` when disabled and `data-focusable` when it stays focusable when disabled | `className` (`pn-ToolbarButton`, then the caller's), `ref`, `disabled`, `data-color` from `color` (default included), `data-icon-only` when it has a `startIcon` and no `children`, and the icon and label spans | `render`, `nativeButton`, `focusableWhenDisabled`, `style`, `onClick`, `aria-label` and every other prop of a native `<button>`, through `{...rest}` |
| `Toolbar.Group`     | `<div role="group">`, with `data-orientation` and, when disabled, `data-disabled`                                                           | `className` (`pn-ToolbarGroup`, then the caller's), `ref`, `disabled`                                                                                                                                            | `render`, `style`, `aria-label` and every other prop of a `<div>`, through `{...rest}`                                                               |
| `Toolbar.Separator` | `<div role="separator" aria-orientation>`, its orientation the opposite of the toolbar's, with `data-orientation`                           | `className` (`pn-ToolbarSeparator`, then the caller's), `ref`                                                                                                                                                    | `orientation`, `render`, `style` and every other prop of a `<div>`, through `{...rest}`                                                              |

Base UI already does: one tab stop for the whole toolbar, a roving `tabIndex` (0 on the item last focused, −1 on the rest), so Tab enters and leaves the bar in one step and comes back to the item it left; the arrow keys of the toolbar's orientation move between items, wrapping at the ends while `loopFocus` is on; the pointer moving over an item makes it the tab stop; a disabled `Toolbar.Root` or `Toolbar.Group` disables every button inside it; a disabled `Toolbar.Button` stays focusable by default (`focusableWhenDisabled` is `true`), with `aria-disabled` in place of `disabled` and its clicks stopped, so it stays in the arrow-key order and can carry a tooltip; a disabled button that isn't focusable leaves the arrow-key order; `Toolbar.Separator` sets its orientation across the toolbar's; Left and Right swap only under Base UI's `DirectionProvider` set to `rtl`, not from the `dir` attribute, and Perron doesn't set one up yet, as all four locales run left to right; `render` on `Toolbar.Button` makes a popup trigger (`Menu.Trigger`, `Popover.Trigger`, `Dialog.Trigger`) one element that joins the arrow-key order and keeps its popup behaviour, passing `disabled` on to it.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop here gets this description as its JSDoc. Slots come last.

`Toolbar` passes Base UI's `orientation` (default `'horizontal'`, for the map's vertical column of controls) and `disabled` through as its own props, and inherits `loopFocus` (default `true`) with its Base UI JSDoc.

### Toolbar

| Name                        | Type                         | Default        | Base UI prop         | Description                                                                                                                   |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------- | -------------- | -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `orientation`               | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` | `orientation`        | Which way the bar runs, and so which arrow keys move through it: Left and Right for `horizontal`, Up and Down for `vertical`. |
| `disabled`                  | `boolean`                    | `false`        | `disabled`           | Whether every button in the toolbar is disabled. The buttons stay focusable unless their `focusableWhenDisabled` is `false`.  |
| `loopFocus`                 | `boolean`                    | `true`         | `loopFocus`          | Inherited from Base UI with its JSDoc: whether the arrow keys wrap from one end of the toolbar to the other.                  |
| `render`                    | Base UI's `render`           | none           | `render`             | Inherited from Base UI: swaps the root element and keeps the behaviour, the class and the data attributes.                    |
| `children`                  | `ReactNode`                  | none           | none                 | The toolbar's `ToolbarButton`s, `ToolbarGroup`s and `ToolbarSeparator`s, in reading order.                                    |
| `className`, `style`, `ref` | React's                      | none           | `className`, `style` | Reach the root. `className` is merged after `pn-Toolbar`.                                                                     |

The caller names the toolbar with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, which reach the root through `{...rest}`; Toolbar declares neither.

### ToolbarButton

`ToolbarButton` has one size, no `size` or `variant` prop, and a quiet neutral look: `size.control` tall and at least as wide, transparent at rest in `color.text.primary`, `color.surface.hover` on hover and press, as the toolbar's glass already marks the bar. `size.control` is the height of icon buttons and filter chips, so a toolbar of icon buttons matches the IconButtons beside it.

`ToolbarButton`'s `color` offers `'neutral' | 'brand'`, the contract's two intents for a toolbar's buttons, with `brand` drawn as a solid brand button (`color.surface.brand` with a `color.border.brand` edge and `color.text.on-color.dark`, `color.surface.brand-hover` on hover and press).

A `ToolbarButton` with a `startIcon` and no `children` is an icon-only button: square (`size.control` both ways, no inline padding), marked `data-icon-only`, and named by the caller's `aria-label`, which its JSDoc requires. The map's zoom and locate controls are icons alone, and the `props` check would not read a union type that enforces the label.

| Name                        | Type                   | Default     | Base UI prop            | Description                                                                                                                                                   |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------- | ----------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `color`                     | `'neutral' \| 'brand'` | `'neutral'` | none                    | The intent: `neutral` is ink on the toolbar's glass, for every action but the main one; `brand` is the brand yellow, for the one main action of a screen.     |
| `disabled`                  | `boolean`              | `false`     | `disabled`              | Whether the button ignores the pointer and the keys. It stays focusable, and in the arrow-key order, unless `focusableWhenDisabled` is `false`.               |
| `startIcon`                 | `ReactNode`            | none        | none                    | An icon before the label, in reading order. Hidden from screen readers. Alone, with no `children`, it makes an icon-only button, which needs an `aria-label`. |
| `endIcon`                   | `ReactNode`            | none        | none                    | An icon after the label, in reading order. Hidden from screen readers: the label names the button.                                                            |
| `focusableWhenDisabled`     | `boolean`              | `true`      | `focusableWhenDisabled` | Inherited from Base UI with its JSDoc: whether the button stays focusable when disabled.                                                                      |
| `nativeButton`              | `boolean`              | `true`      | `nativeButton`          | Inherited from Base UI with its JSDoc: set it to `false` when `render` gives an element that isn't a `<button>`.                                              |
| `render`                    | Base UI's `render`     | none        | `render`                | Inherited from Base UI: swaps the element, such as for a popup's trigger (`render={<Menu.Trigger />}`), which then joins the toolbar's arrow-key order.       |
| `children`                  | `ReactNode`            | none        | none                    | The label: the words that name the action, in sentence case. Leave it out only for an icon-only button with an `aria-label`.                                  |
| `className`, `style`, `ref` | React's                | none        | `className`, `style`    | Reach the root. `className` is merged after `pn-ToolbarButton`.                                                                                               |

### ToolbarGroup

| Name                        | Type               | Default | Base UI prop         | Description                                                                                                |
| --------------------------- | ------------------ | ------- | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `disabled`                  | `boolean`          | `false` | `disabled`           | Whether every button in the group is disabled.                                                             |
