| `render`                    | Base UI's `render` | none    | `render`             | Inherited from Base UI: swaps the root element and keeps the behaviour, the class and the data attributes. |
| `children`                  | `ReactNode`        | none    | none                 | The group's `ToolbarButton`s, in reading order.                                                            |
| `className`, `style`, `ref` | React's            | none    | `className`, `style` | Reach the root. `className` is merged after `pn-ToolbarGroup`.                                             |

### ToolbarSeparator

| Name                        | Type                         | Default                          | Base UI prop         | Description                                                                                                |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------- | -------------------------------- | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `orientation`               | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | Across the toolbar's orientation | `orientation`        | Inherited from Base UI with its JSDoc: the separator's own orientation.                                    |
| `render`                    | Base UI's `render`           | none                             | `render`             | Inherited from Base UI: swaps the root element and keeps the behaviour, the class and the data attributes. |
| `className`, `style`, `ref` | React's                      | none                             | `className`, `style` | Reach the root. `className` is merged after `pn-ToolbarSeparator`.                                         |

No `slotProps`: each of the four components renders one Base UI part, its own root, which takes the component's own props, and the label and icon spans are not Base UI parts. No label-override props: the toolbar owns no strings.

## Tokens

One row per part, state and property. States are the contract's design states: rest is no selector, hover is `:hover` inside `@media (hover: hover)`, pressed is `:active`, focus is `:focus-visible`, disabled is `[data-disabled]`. Every `color` row on `button` sets the button's `color`, which the label and both icons take, since icons draw in `currentColor`.

The toolbar's root takes the Popups' glass (`color.surface.overlay`, a `backdrop-filter` of `effect.glass-blur` and `effect.glass-saturate`, `shadow.panel`, a `border.width.025` edge in `color.border.subtle`) and their nesting, `radius.lg` padded `space.100` so the buttons' `radius.md` nests, with `space.100` between items. The map's controls and the top bar's groups float over the map, which [Elevation](../foundations/elevation.md#surfaces) says is glass.

`ToolbarSeparator` is a `border.width.025` hairline in `color.border.subtle`, drawn as a border so forced colours keep it, running across the bar and inset `space.100` from the bar's padding at each end. `color.border.subtle` is the dividers' colour, and a divider only decorates.

The toolbar, its group and its separator:

| Part                    | State | Property              | Token                                                  |
| ----------------------- | ----- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `root`                  | rest  | `background-color`    | `color.surface.overlay`                                |
| `root`                  | rest  | `backdrop-filter`     | `effect.glass-blur` (blur) and `effect.glass-saturate` |
| `root`                  | rest  | `box-shadow`          | `shadow.panel`                                         |
| `root`                  | rest  | `border-width`        | `border.width.025`                                     |
| `root`                  | rest  | `border-color`        | `color.border.subtle`                                  |
| `root`                  | rest  | `border-radius`       | `radius.lg`                                            |
| `root`                  | rest  | `padding`             | `space.100`                                            |
| `root`                  | rest  | `gap`                 | `space.100`                                            |
| `group`                 | rest  | `gap`                 | `space.100`                                            |
| `separator`, vertical   | rest  | `border-inline-start` | `border.width.025` in `color.border.subtle`            |
| `separator`, vertical   | rest  | `margin-block`        | `space.100`                                            |
| `separator`, horizontal | rest  | `border-block-start`  | `border.width.025` in `color.border.subtle`            |
| `separator`, horizontal | rest  | `margin-inline`       | `space.100`                                            |

`ToolbarButton`, every colour:

| Part                   | State | Property                    | Token                                                                         |
| ---------------------- | ----- | --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `button`               | rest  | `height`, `min-width`       | `size.control`                                                                |
| `button`               | rest  | `padding-inline`            | `space.300`; 0 when `data-icon-only`                                          |
| `button`               | rest  | `gap`                       | `space.150`                                                                   |
| `button`               | rest  | `border-radius`             | `radius.md`                                                                   |
| `button`               | rest  | `border-width`              | `border.width.025`                                                            |
| `label`                | rest  | `font`, `letter-spacing`    | `typography.label`, with its tracking twin                                    |
| `startIcon`, `endIcon` | rest  | `--perron-icon-size`        | `icon.size.400`                                                               |
| `button` (`focusRing`) | focus | `outline`, `outline-offset` | `focus.width` in `color.border.focus`, `focus.offset` (drawn by `perron.css`) |

`ToolbarButton`, `neutral`:

| Part     | State    | Property           | Token                 |
| -------- | -------- | ------------------ | --------------------- |
| `button` | rest     | `background-color` | `transparent`         |
| `button` | rest     | `border-color`     | `transparent`         |
| `button` | rest     | `color`            | `color.text.primary`  |
| `button` | hover    | `background-color` | `color.surface.hover` |
| `button` | pressed  | `background-color` | `color.surface.hover` |
| `button` | disabled | `background-color` | `transparent`         |
| `button` | disabled | `color`            | `color.text.tertiary` |

`ToolbarButton`, `brand`:

| Part     | State    | Property           | Token                       |
| -------- | -------- | ------------------ | --------------------------- |
| `button` | rest     | `background-color` | `color.surface.brand`       |
| `button` | rest     | `border-color`     | `color.border.brand`        |
| `button` | rest     | `color`            | `color.text.on-color.dark`  |
| `button` | hover    | `background-color` | `color.surface.brand-hover` |
| `button` | pressed  | `background-color` | `color.surface.brand-hover` |
| `button` | disabled | `background-color` | `color.surface.inset`       |
| `button` | disabled | `border-color`     | `transparent`               |
| `button` | disabled | `color`            | `color.text.tertiary`       |

A disabled brand button looks like a disabled neutral one on a fill, `color.surface.inset` with `color.text.tertiary` and no edge: disabled is a colour, and a yellow that can't be pressed shouldn't still mark the main action.

Highlighted, open, selected and invalid don't apply: a toolbar item takes focus rather than `data-highlighted`, a popup trigger rendered through `render` keeps the button's look when its popup is open, and a toolbar holds no choice or value.

## Keyboard and ARIA

From the Base UI reference for `Toolbar` and the installed `ToolbarRoot`, `ToolbarButton`, `ToolbarGroup`, `ToolbarSeparator` and the composite root they build on. "From" says who does it.

| Key                    | Does                                                                                                                                                                                                  | From                                           |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`, `Shift+Tab`     | Moves focus into the toolbar, to the item that last had it (the first enabled item at first), and out of it again: the toolbar is one tab stop                                                        | Base UI                                        |
| `ArrowRight`           | In a horizontal toolbar, moves focus to the next item, wrapping from the last to the first while `loopFocus` is on; the previous item under an `rtl` `DirectionProvider`, which Perron doesn't set up | Base UI                                        |
| `ArrowLeft`            | In a horizontal toolbar, moves focus to the previous item, wrapping from the first to the last while `loopFocus` is on; the next item under an `rtl` `DirectionProvider`, which Perron doesn't set up | Base UI                                        |
| `ArrowDown`, `ArrowUp` | In a vertical toolbar, move focus to the next and the previous item, wrapping while `loopFocus` is on                                                                                                 | Base UI                                        |
| `Enter`, `Space`       | Activate the focused button: fire `onClick`, or open the popup of a trigger given through `render`                                                                                                    | The browser; Base UI for a non-button `render` |

`Home` and `End` do nothing: Base UI's toolbar doesn't turn them on (`enableHomeAndEndKeys` is off in the installed `ToolbarRoot`), and the component adds no keys of its own.

| Element                | Role                                                               | Accessible name from                                                                         | States announced                                                                    |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`                 | `toolbar`, from Base UI                                            | The caller's `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`                                               | `aria-orientation`                                                                  |
| `button`               | `button`, native; `role="button"` when `render` gives a non-button | Its text content, the label's `children`; for an icon-only button, the caller's `aria-label` | Disabled: `aria-disabled` while focusable when disabled, else the native `disabled` |
| `startIcon`, `endIcon` | none: `aria-hidden="true"`                                         | none                                                                                         | none                                                                                |
| `group`                | `group`, from Base UI                                              | The caller's `aria-label`, when the group needs one                                          | none                                                                                |
| `separator`            | `separator`, from Base UI                                          | none                                                                                         | `aria-orientation`, across the toolbar's                                            |

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: a button's label is the text it is named by, and an icon-only button's `aria-label` says what its icon shows; the icons are `aria-hidden`; `color` carries emphasis, not meaning; disabled is announced by `aria-disabled` or `disabled`; the separator is announced as one.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: the toolbar is named by the caller's `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, which every story sets, so two toolbars on a screen tell themselves apart.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: none here; the toolbar owns no strings.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: a button's `children`, `startIcon` and `endIcon` render a string, an element and a list alike, in both colours and both orientations.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; the toolbar keeps no hidden copy and collapses nothing.
- [ ] Native semantics first: native `<button>`s from `Toolbar.Button`, and Base UI's `toolbar`, `group` and `separator` roles, with ARIA only for the toolbar's and an icon-only button's names.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: the arrow keys move through the items in document order, swapped only under an `rtl` `DirectionProvider`, which Perron doesn't set up, and the toolbar opens nothing of its own; a popup opened through `render` returns focus to its trigger, by Base UI.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: the smallest target is an icon-only button, `size.control` (34 px) square.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; the toolbar has no loop and no transition.

## Owned strings

No owned strings: every word comes from the caller, as a button's `children`, an icon-only button's `aria-label`, or the toolbar's `aria-label`.

## Component rules

Rules for this component alone, numbered so the build and the review can cite them.

- **CR-1.** Base UI's toolbar already gives the one tab stop, the roving `tabIndex`, the arrow keys, the wrap and the disabled cascade from root and group to button, so the components rebuild none of it and add no key handlers.
- **CR-2.** `ToolbarButton`, `ToolbarGroup` and `ToolbarSeparator` only render inside a `Toolbar`: Base UI's parts read its context. Every story renders them in one.
- **CR-3.** Each of the four takes `{...rest}` before its own attributes and its own props out of `rest` first (`orientation`, `disabled`, `color`, `startIcon`, `endIcon`; an inherited Base UI prop such as `loopFocus` stays in `rest`, keeping Base UI's default), and merges `className` after its own `pn-` class; `ref` reaches its one element.
- **CR-4.** `ToolbarButton`'s root always carries `data-color`, default included, and `data-icon-only` when it has a `startIcon` and no `children`; the CSS selects on them, one class then attributes: `.pn-ToolbarButton[data-color='brand']`. The toolbar's layout reads Base UI's `data-orientation`: `.pn-Toolbar[data-orientation='vertical']` is a column.
- **CR-5.** The states keep the button's geometry: hover, pressed, focus and disabled change colours only, never the height, padding, gap, border width or radius. Every button draws a `border.width.025` border, `transparent` on a neutral button and a disabled brand one, so both colours share one size and Windows' forced colours draw an edge round each.
- **CR-6.** Hover is read inside `@media (hover: hover)`; pressed (`:active`) takes the hover tokens in a rule outside it, so a touch press shows. Neither applies to a disabled button: both rules exclude `[data-disabled]`, since a button focusable when disabled has no native `disabled` and still matches `:hover` and `:active`.
- **CR-7.** Focus uses the ring `perron.css` draws on `:focus-visible`; the component draws no ring of its own and never removes the outline. The root's `space.100` padding and gap leave the ring, `focus.offset` plus `focus.width` out, inside the bar.
- **CR-8.** The colour is set on the button's `color`; the label and the icons take it through `currentColor`. No rule sets a colour on an icon. The icon spans are `aria-hidden="true"`, rendered only when their prop is given, and set `--perron-icon-size` to `icon.size.400`.
- **CR-9.** A button's label stays on one line (`white-space: nowrap`), the button growing with it, rather than wrapping inside the fixed `size.control` height.
- **CR-10.** A `brand` button keeps its `color.border.brand` edge at rest, on hover and pressed: the light-theme yellow fill reaches only 2.1:1 on the surfaces, and the edge carries the 3:1 ([Semantic colours](../foundations/semantic-colours.md#brand)).
- **CR-11.** The separator is drawn as a border on a box of no size (`border-inline-start` across a horizontal toolbar, `border-block-start` across a vertical one), stretched across the bar with `align-self: stretch`, never as a background, which forced colours remove.
- **CR-12.** Changes of state are immediate: no `duration.*` token fits a button's state change, so the CSS has no transition.
- **CR-13.** The toolbar sizes to its content (`display: inline-flex`); placing it on the map, its `z-index` and its distance from the edge belong to the pattern that uses it, such as MapControls.

## Stories

The deferred design's page draws two components: the toolbar, with one variant property, `orientation` (`horizontal`, `vertical`), and its button, with `color` (`neutral`, `brand`) and `State` (`default`, `hover`, `focus`, `disabled`). Each story is named by its variant name (`penpot/README.md`, "Conventions").

The button's stories, and a later drawing's exports, are prefixed `Button`, as `ButtonNeutralDefault`, beside the toolbar's `Horizontal` and `Vertical`, since the Penpot conventions name a variant by its property values alone.

The toolbar stories render a toolbar named "Map controls" (zoom in, zoom out, a separator, then a group with "Show whole line" and a brand "Show departures"), with `packages/perron/icons/`'s `plus`, `minus` and `locate`. The button stories render one labelled button, "Show whole line", in a toolbar named "Actions", and set `disabled` for a `Disabled` story. The hover and focus stories render at rest: the visual check drives the state, and their `play` tests check it.

| Story                   | Shows                                                                                           | `play` test                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Horizontal`            | horizontal toolbar: two icon-only buttons, a separator, a group of two labelled buttons         | Tab focuses the first button; ArrowRight moves through each button, skipping the separator, and wraps to the first; ArrowLeft goes back; Enter fires `onClick` once; Shift+Tab leaves, and Tab returns to the last focused button |
| `Vertical`              | vertical toolbar: zoom in, zoom out, a separator, locate, all icon-only                         | ArrowDown and ArrowUp move between the buttons and ArrowRight doesn't; the separator's `aria-orientation` is `horizontal`                                                                                                         |
| `ButtonNeutralDefault`  | neutral button, at rest                                                                         | none                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `ButtonNeutralHover`    | neutral button, hover                                                                           | Hovering lays `color.surface.hover` over the transparent fill                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `ButtonNeutralFocus`    | neutral button, focus                                                                           | Tab gives the button `:focus-visible` and the ring                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `ButtonNeutralDisabled` | neutral button, disabled                                                                        | The button has `aria-disabled` and `data-disabled`, Tab still reaches it, and a click fires no `onClick`                                                                                                                          |
| `ButtonBrandDefault`    | brand button, at rest                                                                           | none                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `ButtonBrandHover`      | brand button, hover                                                                             | Hovering sets the `color.surface.brand-hover` fill and keeps the `color.border.brand` edge                                                                                                                                        |
| `ButtonBrandFocus`      | brand button, focus                                                                             | none                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `ButtonBrandDisabled`   | brand button, disabled                                                                          | none                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `IconOnly`              | horizontal toolbar of three icon-only neutral buttons, two given `false` and `''` as `children` | Each button is named by its `aria-label`, has `data-icon-only` and no label span, its icon span is `aria-hidden`, and it is `size.control` square                                                                                 |
| `Disabled`              | horizontal toolbar with `disabled`                                                              | Every button carries `data-disabled`, the arrow keys still move between them, and a click fires no `onClick`                                                                                                                      |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                                                       | Don't                                                                                                                                |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Name every toolbar with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, such as "Map controls", so a screen reader tells it from the next one                         | Leave a toolbar unnamed: two on a screen are both announced as "toolbar"                                                             |
| Put each action in a `ToolbarButton`, so the arrow keys reach it                                                                                         | Put a Button, an IconButton or a plain `<button>` straight into the toolbar: it falls out of the arrow-key order and adds a tab stop |
| Give an icon-only button an `aria-label` that names the action: "Zoom in"                                                                                | Leave an icon-only button without one: its icon is `aria-hidden`, so the button has no name                                          |
| Open a menu, popover or dialog through `render`, `<ToolbarButton render={<Menu.Trigger />}>`, and set `disabled` on the `ToolbarButton`, not the trigger | Disable the trigger itself: Base UI says the button then leaves the toolbar's arrow-key order                                        |
| Wrap a button in a tooltip with `<Tooltip.Trigger render={<ToolbarButton … />} />`, the way round Base UI gives for tooltips                             | Pass the tooltip's trigger to `ToolbarButton`'s `render`, as for popups                                                              |
| Give one button per screen `color="brand"`, for its main action                                                                                          | Mark several toolbar buttons `brand`, or use it for emphasis: a second yellow action leaves neither the main one                     |
| Keep a disabled button focusable, the default, so it can explain itself through a tooltip                                                                | Restyle a disabled button with `opacity`: disabled is `color.text.tertiary`, a colour                                                |
| Use a SegmentedControl or FilterChips for a choice or an on-and-off filter                                                                               | Build a toggle out of a `ToolbarButton`: it draws no selected state                                                                  |
| Place the toolbar over the map in a pattern, which sets its position and stacking                                                                        | Set a `z-index` or a margin from the screen edge on the toolbar itself: the component sizes to its content                           |

# EmptyState

Stands in for a list or panel that has nothing to show, and says in plain words what is empty, why, and what to try next.

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`): this spec decides what the drawing would, from the [contract](README.md), the [foundations](../foundations/README.md), [content design](../content-design.md) and the tokens. EmptyState has no Base UI component and nothing in `dependsOn`.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/EmptyState`. Family: none, since it is static content that sits on its container's surface and joins no family's treatment. Shared parts: none.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                             | Base UI part                          | Class                       | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | A `div` stacking the parts below in a centred column                                                   | None: `useRender`, a `div` by default | `pn-EmptyState`             | none            |
| `icon`              | A `div` holding the caller's `icon`, hidden from screen readers; rendered only when given              | None: `useRender`, a `div` by default | `pn-EmptyState-icon`        | `icon`          |
| `title`             | A `p` holding the caller's `title`: what is empty                                                      | None: `useRender`, a `p` by default   | `pn-EmptyState-title`       | `title`         |
| `description`       | A `div` holding the caller's `children`: why, and what to try; rendered only when given                | None: `useRender`, a `div` by default | `pn-EmptyState-description` | `description`   |
| `action`            | A `div` holding the caller's `action`, such as a button that clears a filter; rendered only when given | None: `useRender`, a `div` by default | `pn-EmptyState-action`      | `action`        |

No part has a Base UI component, because none has behaviour for Base UI to give: no focus, keys, state or popup. Each part renders through Base UI's `useRender` hook instead, so each takes `render`, as the root does and as its `slotProps` key does for an inner part.

- Decided: the title renders as a `p` by default, with no heading level of its own; a caller that wants it in the page's outline makes it a heading through `slotProps.title.render`, such as `render: <h3 />`. EmptyState sits inside panels whose heading levels it cannot know, and a wrong level breaks the outline where a `p` leaves it whole.

## Base UI parts

No Base UI component: each part renders through the `useRender` hook from `@base-ui/react/use-render`, and merges its props with `mergeProps` from `@base-ui/react/merge-props`, at the version pinned in `packages/perron/package.json` (1.9.0).

| Base UI part                | Renders | Perron sets                                                                                      | Passed through                                                        |
| --------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `useRender` for root        | `div`   | `defaultTagName: 'div'`, `ref`, the class `pn-EmptyState`, and the parts below as children       | `render`, `className`, `style`, `ref` and the rest of the `div` props |
| `useRender` for icon        | `div`   | `defaultTagName: 'div'`, the class `pn-EmptyState-icon`, `aria-hidden: true`, `icon` as children | `slotProps.icon`                                                      |
| `useRender` for title       | `p`     | `defaultTagName: 'p'`, the class `pn-EmptyState-title`, `title` as children                      | `slotProps.title`, its `render` making it a heading                   |
| `useRender` for description | `div`   | `defaultTagName: 'div'`, the class `pn-EmptyState-description`, `children` as children           | `slotProps.description`                                               |
| `useRender` for action      | `div`   | `defaultTagName: 'div'`, the class `pn-EmptyState-action`, `action` as children                  | `slotProps.action`                                                    |

Base UI already does: swapping each part's element through `render` while keeping its class and props, joining `className` strings and `style` objects and chaining event handlers in `mergeProps`, and setting `ref` on the rendered element.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop here gets this description as its JSDoc. Slots come last.

| Name                    | Type                              | Default | Base UI prop                | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `title`                 | `ReactNode`                       |         | none                        | What is empty, in a few words: "No matches for Nørrebro st". Required. Replaces the HTML `title` attribute                                                                                                                                                               |
| `children`              | `ReactNode`                       |         | none                        | The sentence under the title: why it is empty and what to try. "Try a line number such as 5C."                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `icon`                  | `ReactNode`                       |         | none                        | An icon from Perron's set above the title, for the eye only: it is hidden from screen readers. It renders at 16 px, `icon.size.400`; for an icon drawn for another step, set `--perron-icon-size` to that step's `icon.size.*` on the icon part through `slotProps.icon` |
| `action`                | `ReactNode`                       |         | none                        | What the person can do about it, such as a button that clears the search, below the sentence                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `render`                | Base UI's `render`                |         | inherited                   | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.                                                                                |
| `className`             | `string`                          |         | none                        | Joined after `pn-EmptyState` on the root                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `style`                 | `CSSProperties`                   |         | none                        | Reaches the root                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `ref`                   | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>`             |         | none                        | Reaches the root element                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `slotProps.icon`        | `useRender.ComponentProps<'div'>` |         | `useRender` for icon        | Props for the `icon` part                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `slotProps.title`       | `useRender.ComponentProps<'p'>`   |         | `useRender` for title       | Props for the `title` part. Its `render` makes the title a heading: `render: <h3 />`                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `slotProps.description` | `useRender.ComponentProps<'div'>` |         | `useRender` for description | Props for the `description` part                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `slotProps.action`      | `useRender.ComponentProps<'div'>` |         | `useRender` for action      | Props for the `action` part                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

`render`, `className`, `style`, `ref` and the other `div` props reach the root, as the contract's Root section says; `render` is inherited from `useRender` as it is, with Base UI's JSDoc, and `EmptyStateProps` does not declare it again. No owned string, so no `*Label` prop.

- Decided: `children` is the sentence under the title, the way MUI's `Alert` takes its message, rather than a separate `description` prop, so the common call reads `<EmptyState title="No departures in the next hour">Nothing leaves this stop in the next hour.</EmptyState>`. The part keeps the name `description` for its class and `slotProps` key.
- Decided: the names `title`, `icon` and `action` are taken from MUI (`CardHeader`'s `title`, `Alert`'s `icon` and `action`), and `title` is taken out of the root's props so the HTML `title` attribute never reaches the element; an EmptyState has no use for a hover tooltip.
- Decided: EmptyState ships with no `variant`, `size` or `color`, one look everywhere. The uses known now (an empty search, an empty list in a sheet, a data panel with nothing to show) share one calm look, and any of the three can join later as an optional prop without a break.

## Tokens

One row per part, state and property. EmptyState has no interactive state of its own, so every row is rest; the caller's action keeps its own states.

| Part          | State | Property             | Token                                 |
| ------------- | ----- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `root`        | rest  | `padding-block`      | `space.600`                           |
| `root`        | rest  | `padding-inline`     | `space.400`                           |
| `root`        | rest  | `gap`                | `space.100`                           |
| `icon`        | rest  | `color`              | `color.text.secondary`                |
| `icon`        | rest  | `margin-block-end`   | `space.200`                           |
| `icon`        | rest  | `--perron-icon-size` | `icon.size.400`                       |
| `title`       | rest  | `font`               | `typography.heading-sm`               |
| `title`       | rest  | `letter-spacing`     | `typography.heading-sm`, its tracking |
| `title`       | rest  | `color`              | `color.text.primary`                  |
| `description` | rest  | `font`               | `typography.body-sm`                  |
| `description` | rest  | `letter-spacing`     | `typography.body-sm`, its tracking    |
| `description` | rest  | `color`              | `color.text.secondary`                |
| `action`      | rest  | `gap`                | `space.200`                           |
| `action`      | rest  | `margin-block-start` | `space.300`                           |

The root is a flex column with `align-items: center` and `text-align: center`; the action is a flex row that wraps, centred. The spacing comes out as 12 px from icon to title (`space.100` and `space.200`), 4 px from title to sentence, and 16 px from sentence to action (`space.100` and `space.300`). Every part and the root reset the margins a `p` brings, and the icon part is a flex box so an inline SVG adds no baseline gap below it.

- Decided: the root has no fill, border, radius or shadow, so EmptyState takes the surface of the panel, sheet or popup it sits in. It is content, not a card, and a surface of its own would join no family and stack a box inside a box.
- Decided: the layout is a centred column, padded `space.600` on the block axis and `space.400` on the inline axis, with the gaps in the table above. Centred is how an empty list reads at a glance in a narrow sheet, 24 px matches the space between blocks of a pane, and 16 px inline keeps text clear of a 320 px screen's edges.
- Decided: the icon is a bare icon from Perron's set, in `color.text.secondary`, with no disc or tile behind it, and the icon part sets `--perron-icon-size` to `icon.size.400`, the 16 px step the set's default icons are drawn for, as the contract sizes an icon on the element that holds it. An icon drawn for another step gets that step's `icon.size.*` through `slotProps.icon`, by `className` or `style`; a larger icon needs a new drawing, as the icon foundation's Sizes section says, never a scaled one. The brand keeps the interface calm, and a disc would need a size token no foundation gives it.
- Decided: the title is `typography.heading-sm` in `color.text.primary`, and the sentence `typography.body-sm` in `color.text.secondary`. The roles' own uses are "card titles" and "the line under a title", and both colours meet 4.5:1 on every surface.

## Keyboard and ARIA

EmptyState has no keys of its own and is never focusable. The caller's action is reached in reading order.

| Key         | Does                                                                   | From        |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `Tab`       | Moves to the first focusable element in the action, after the sentence | The browser |
| `Shift+Tab` | Moves back out of the action, to whatever came before the EmptyState   | The browser |

| Element       | Role                                                               | Accessible name from             | States announced |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `root`        | None (generic `div`)                                               | None                             | None             |
| `icon`        | Hidden: `aria-hidden="true"`                                       | None                             | None             |
| `title`       | Paragraph, or a heading when `slotProps.title.render` makes it one | Its text, from `title`           | None             |
| `description` | None (generic `div`)                                               | None                             | None             |
| `action`      | None (generic `div`); the caller's controls carry their own roles  | The caller's controls' own names | Theirs           |

- Decided: the root carries no live-region role, leaving the caller to add `role="status"` when the EmptyState replaces results while the person types or filters. An empty state shown with the page on load needs no announcement, the accessibility rules ask for live regions on changes of state only, and a search field such as SearchField announces its own empty results.

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the icon is `aria-hidden` and decorative, and the title, read as text, says what the icon shows.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: none here; the root is not a landmark or region.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: none here; EmptyState owns no string.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `title`, `children`, `icon` and `action` each render a string, an element and an array; `description` and `action` are `div`s, so block content such as a list is valid inside them, and the title takes phrasing content as a `p` or a heading does.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; nothing animates or collapses.
- [ ] Native semantics first: a `p` for the title, made a native `h2` to `h6` through `render` when it heads a section; the action holds the caller's own `button` or `a href`.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: the action follows the sentence in the DOM and on screen; EmptyState never moves focus when it appears, and nothing in it closes.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: EmptyState has no target of its own; the action's targets are the caller's components, which keep their own sizes.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; nothing moves.

## Owned strings

No owned strings: every word EmptyState shows comes from the caller, through `title`, `children` and `action`, and the icon is hidden from screen readers.

## Component rules

Rules for this component alone, numbered so the build and the review can cite them.

- **CR-1.** The optional parts render only when given: no `icon` part without `icon`, no `description` part without `children`, no `action` part without `action`. A value that renders nothing (`null`, `undefined`, a boolean, `''`, or an array of only such values) counts as not given, so no empty wrapper takes up a gap.
- **CR-2.** The `icon` part always carries `aria-hidden="true"`, after the caller's `slotProps.icon` props, so those props cannot make the icon speak; the title says what it shows. A `render` element's own props are the caller's: `useRender` merges them last, as Base UI does, so a caller that swaps the icon's element leaves `aria-hidden` off it.
- **CR-3.** `title`, `icon`, `action`, `children`, `slotProps` and `render` are taken out of the rest props before they reach the root, so the HTML `title` attribute never reaches the element.
- **CR-4.** Each inner part's props are its `slotProps` value merged with `mergeProps`, the component's own props last, so its class, `aria-hidden` and children stay while the caller's `className` joins and its `render` swaps the element.
- **CR-5.** EmptyState never moves focus, sets no `tabindex` and adds no role to the root; the caller decides whether it is announced.
- **CR-6.** It sizes to its container, with no width or max-width of its own, and long words wrap (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`), so a long Danish stop name in the title fits a 320 px screen.
- **CR-7.** Colour sits on the parts that hold text, and the icon takes `currentColor` from its part, as the icon foundation asks.

## Stories

One per variant and state the Penpot design shows, named as Penpot names it. The design is deferred and has no variant property, so its one variant is `Default`; `TitleOnly` is the same variant with the optional props left out, and proves CR-1.

| Story       | Shows                                                                                                                                                                                  | `play` test                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Default`   | Every part: the `search` icon, `title` "No matches for Nørrebro st", the sentence "Try a line number such as 5C." and an action, an `outline` `neutral` Button "Clear search", at rest | The icon part is `aria-hidden`; Tab reaches the "Clear search" button and Shift+Tab leaves it, so focus ends where it started                             |
| `TitleOnly` | `title` "No departures in the next hour", with no icon, sentence or action                                                                                                             | Only the root and the title render: no `pn-EmptyState-icon`, `pn-EmptyState-description` or `pn-EmptyState-action` element, and nothing in it takes focus |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                                                                                     | Don't                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Say what is empty, then what to try, in plain sentences: "No matches for Nørrebro st" over "Try a line number such as 5C."                                                             | Write "Oops! Nothing here!": content design has no exclamation marks, and the title should name what is missing                             |
| Say only what the data knows: "No departures in the next hour" when the timetable covers an hour                                                                                       | Write "No departures" when there may be some later: the brand never claims more certainty than the data has                                 |
| Use it for a list, a search or a panel with nothing in it                                                                                                                              | Use it for loading or for missing real-time data: loading says "Loading", and missing data uses the data-state words such as "No signal"    |
| Give one neutral action at most, such as clearing the search or the filters                                                                                                            | Add a `brand` action when the panel already has one: a screen has one brand action at most                                                  |
| Pick a decorative icon from Perron's set that matches the title, or none; it renders at 16 px, and one drawn for another step takes that step's `icon.size.*` through `slotProps.icon` | Let the icon carry meaning alone, or use an emoji: the icon is hidden from screen readers and Mylder uses no emoji                          |
| Make the title a heading through `slotProps.title.render` when the EmptyState stands in for a whole section                                                                            | Wrap the title in your own heading element inside `title`: the part is a `p` until `render` swaps it, and a heading inside a `p` is invalid |
| Add `role="status"` on the root when it replaces results as the person types or filters, so the change is announced                                                                    | Add a live region to an EmptyState shown on load: there is no change to announce, and it adds noise                                         |

title: Surface
markdown:
# Surface

A box that sets content on one step of the surface ladder: glass or an opaque panel floating over the map, a raised card inside a panel, or an inset box, each with its fill, edge, radius, shadow and padding from the tokens.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/Surface`. Family: none. Shared parts: none.

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`), so this spec decides the drawing: the layers below are the ones the drawing will name, and the variants are the steps of the surface ladder on [Elevation](../foundations/elevation.md#surfaces). Surface has no Base UI part: it is a box with no behaviour, so its root renders through Base UI's `useRender` hook (`@base-ui/react/use-render`), which gives it the `render` prop.

Surface is not one of the contract's [families](README.md#families): it is the box the ladder is drawn on, which patterns such as a detail panel or a disruption card compose. Its `glass` variant draws the Panels row's treatment (the Popups' glass, `radius.xl`), so a panel a pattern builds from it matches the Dialog and Sheet beside it.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                                       | Base UI part                            | Class        | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------- | ------------ | --------------- |
| `root`              | The box: a `<div>` with the variant's fill, edge, radius, shadow and padding, holding the caller's content. Penpot's main instance, a flex board | none: a `<div>` rendered by `useRender` | `pn-Surface` | none            |

The content is the caller's: Surface draws no heading, divider or inner part, so the drawing's one layer is `root`, holding a placeholder content slot that the code map does not map to a part.

Surface's one Penpot variant property is `variant`, with the values `raised`, `inset`, `glass` and `opaque` in that order, so `raised` is the default (the contract's first value), and the variants are `Raised`, `Inset`, `Glass` and `Opaque`. They are the four steps of [Elevation](../foundations/elevation.md#surfaces) a box sits on, named by what they look like rather than by their token (`overlay` and `default` would collide with the floating-panel words and with Penpot's `State` value `default`); `raised` comes first because cards inside a panel are the commonest box, and a floating panel is usually a pattern that chooses `glass` on purpose. `color.surface.hover`, `selected`, `inverse` and the tinted intent surfaces are state layers, buttons and messages, not boxes, so they are not variants.

## Base UI parts

Surface imports no Base UI component. It uses two Base UI utilities, at the version pinned in `package.json`: `useRender` (`@base-ui/react/use-render`) for the root and `mergeProps` (`@base-ui/react/merge-props`) to merge the caller's props with its own.

| Base UI part                     | Renders | Perron sets                                                                                                              | Passed through                                                    |
| -------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `useRender` (a hook, not a part) | `<div>` | `defaultTagName: 'div'`, `className` (`pn-Surface` first, then the caller's), `data-variant` from `variant` (CR-1, CR-2) | `render`, `ref`, `children`, `className`, `style`, the rest props |

Base UI already does: swapping the root element for the one `render` gives, keeping the class and data attribute; merging the caller's `ref` with the element's; and merging event handlers, `className` and `style` through `mergeProps`.

Surface renders a `<div>` by default, with no role, and leaves a landmark or region to the caller through `render` (`render={<section aria-labelledby="…" />}`, `<aside>`, `<article>`). Most surfaces are cards and boxes inside a panel, which are not landmarks; a `<section>` or `<aside>` by default would add an unnamed region to every card, and the contract asks every landmark and named region for a name only the caller's heading can give.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop Surface declares gets this description as its JSDoc. It declares `variant`, `children`, `className`, `style` and `ref`, and inherits `render` from `useRender`'s props type as it is, with Base UI's description; a caller renders it as `<section>` or `<aside>` with `aria-labelledby` for a named region. Surface has no `slotProps`, because the contract keys `slotProps` by inner Base UI part and Surface has none; a caller restyles it through `className` on the root.

| Name                 | Type                                         | Default    | Base UI prop         | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ---------- | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `variant`            | `'raised' \| 'inset' \| 'glass' \| 'opaque'` | `'raised'` | none                 | The step of the surface ladder: `raised` for a card inside a panel, `inset` for a box or track set into one, `glass` for a panel floating over the map, `opaque` for a floating panel full of text on a phone, where glass would let the map show through. |
| `render`             | Base UI's `render`                           |            | inherited            | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.                                                                  |
| `children`           | `ReactNode`                                  |            | none                 | The content the surface holds                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `className`, `style` | React's                                      |            | through `mergeProps` | Reach the root; `className` is merged after `pn-Surface`                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `ref`                | `Ref<HTMLElement>`                           |            | `useRender`'s `ref`  | Reaches the root element, whichever element `render` makes it                                                                                                                                                                                              |

No `size`: padding follows the variant (see [Tokens](#tokens)). No label props: Surface owns no strings.

Surface has no `color`, so no variant is tinted with an intent's surface (`color.surface.success` and the rest). A tinted box says something only colour tells, and colour is never alone ([Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#rules)): a status surface belongs to a component that also gives the word or icon, such as a notice, which can add the tints then. `color` can join Surface later without a break.

## Tokens

Surface is not interactive, so its one design state is rest; each row names the `variant` it applies to. Every variant has the same edge width, so the four share one geometry and swapping variants never shifts the content.

Each variant takes the treatment below: `raised` a `color.surface.raised` card with a `color.border.subtle` edge, `radius.lg` and no shadow; `inset` a `color.surface.inset` box with a transparent edge and `radius.lg`; `glass` the Panels' glass (`color.surface.overlay`, the glass blur and saturation, a `color.border.subtle` edge, `shadow.panel`) at `radius.xl`; and `opaque` the same as glass with `color.surface.default` and no blur. It is [Elevation](../foundations/elevation.md) and [Semantic spacing](../foundations/semantic-spacing.md) as written: floating panels are glass with `shadow.panel` and `radius.xl`, and on phones opaque; cards and inset boxes take `radius.lg`; card and panel edges are `border.width.025` in `color.border.subtle`; an inset box reads without a border; and nothing else casts a shadow.

Surface pads its content by variant, `space.400` for `glass` and `opaque` and `space.300` for `raised` and `inset`, with no prop to change it, so a caller who needs another inset (rows running to the edge, a flush image) sets `padding` through `className` with a `space.*` token. A box with no padding is never used as it comes, and a padding prop would grow a scale before any caller needs one; `space.300` is the gap between parts of a detail panel, and a floating panel one step wider sets its blocks off from the map. A `padding` prop can join later without a break.

| Part   | State                    | Property           | Token                                                                                                                                  |
| ------ | ------------------------ | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root` | rest, every `variant`    | `color`            | `color.text.primary`                                                                                                                   |
| `root` | rest, every `variant`    | `border-width`     | `border.width.025`                                                                                                                     |
| `root` | rest, every `variant`    | `border-style`     | none: the keyword `solid`                                                                                                              |
| `root` | rest, `variant='raised'` | `background-color` | `color.surface.raised`                                                                                                                 |
| `root` | rest, `variant='raised'` | `border-color`     | `color.border.subtle`                                                                                                                  |
| `root` | rest, `variant='raised'` | `border-radius`    | `radius.lg`                                                                                                                            |
| `root` | rest, `variant='raised'` | `padding`          | `space.300`                                                                                                                            |
| `root` | rest, `variant='raised'` | `box-shadow`       | none: the keyword `none`                                                                                                               |
| `root` | rest, `variant='inset'`  | `background-color` | `color.surface.inset`                                                                                                                  |
| `root` | rest, `variant='inset'`  | `border-color`     | none: the keyword `transparent`, so the edge shows only in forced colours (CR-5)                                                       |
| `root` | rest, `variant='inset'`  | `border-radius`    | `radius.lg`                                                                                                                            |
| `root` | rest, `variant='inset'`  | `padding`          | `space.300`                                                                                                                            |
| `root` | rest, `variant='inset'`  | `box-shadow`       | none: the keyword `none`                                                                                                               |
| `root` | rest, `variant='glass'`  | `background-color` | `color.surface.overlay`                                                                                                                |
| `root` | rest, `variant='glass'`  | `backdrop-filter`  | `effect.glass-blur` and `effect.glass-saturate`: `blur(var(--perron-effect-glass-blur)) saturate(var(--perron-effect-glass-saturate))` |
| `root` | rest, `variant='glass'`  | `border-color`     | `color.border.subtle`                                                                                                                  |
| `root` | rest, `variant='glass'`  | `border-radius`    | `radius.xl`                                                                                                                            |
| `root` | rest, `variant='glass'`  | `padding`          | `space.400`                                                                                                                            |
| `root` | rest, `variant='glass'`  | `box-shadow`       | `shadow.panel`                                                                                                                         |
| `root` | rest, `variant='opaque'` | `background-color` | `color.surface.default`                                                                                                                |
| `root` | rest, `variant='opaque'` | `border-color`     | `color.border.subtle`                                                                                                                  |
| `root` | rest, `variant='opaque'` | `border-radius`    | `radius.xl`                                                                                                                            |
| `root` | rest, `variant='opaque'` | `padding`          | `space.400`                                                                                                                            |
| `root` | rest, `variant='opaque'` | `box-shadow`       | `shadow.panel`                                                                                                                         |

Every text colour reaches 4.5:1 on `color.surface.default`, `raised` and `inset` in both themes, as [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#text-on-surfaces) measures, except `color.text.tertiary`, which stays for hints beside stronger text. The build measures text on the three opaque surfaces only. `color.surface.overlay` is `color.surface.default`'s colour at 0.9 opacity in light and 0.88 in dark, behind the glass blur, so text on `glass` reads close to its contrast on `color.surface.default`.

## Keyboard and ARIA

Surface is a box: it takes no focus, and no key does anything. Focus moves through the caller's content in reading order. A caller who makes it a link or button through `render` brings that element's own keys.

| Key  | Does                                                          | From   |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
| none | Surface is not focusable or operable; Tab reaches its content | Perron |

| Element | Role                    | Accessible name from                                                                                                               | States announced |
| ------- | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `root`  | none: a generic `<div>` | Not named. Through `render`, a `<section>`, `<aside>` or `<article>` takes its name from the caller's heading by `aria-labelledby` | none             |

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the surface tells the eye only grouping and depth, which the content's own headings and order tell the ear; Surface carries no colour that means a state (no `color` prop).
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: the root is a generic `<div>` and no landmark; a caller who renders it as `<section>`, `<aside>` or `<article>` names it with `aria-labelledby` pointing at its heading, as the `Nested` story shows.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: none here; Surface owns no label.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `children` as a string, an element and a list all render in each of the four variants, shown by the variant stories.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; Surface does not animate or collapse.
- [ ] Native semantics first: a `<div>` with no role and no ARIA; the caller picks `<section>`, `<aside>` or `<article>` through `render` when the box is a region.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: Surface takes no focus and does not reorder its content; it does not clip, so a focused child's ring shows in full (CR-4).
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: no target; Surface is not pressed.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; Surface has no motion.

## Owned strings

No owned strings: Surface shows and announces no words of its own; every word inside it is the caller's.

## Component rules

- **CR-1.** The root renders through `useRender` with `defaultTagName: 'div'` and `mergeProps`: Surface's own props (`className` starting with `pn-Surface`, `data-variant`) win over the caller's rest props, and `variant` is taken out of the rest before the merge, so it never reaches the DOM.
- **CR-2.** The root always carries `data-variant` with the `variant` value, `raised` by default, and the CSS reads the treatment from it: `.pn-Surface[data-variant='glass']`.
- **CR-3.** Surface sets no `display`, `inline-size`, `block-size`, `margin`, `gap` or typography: it is a block box that sizes to its container, and its content and the caller's layout decide the rest. It sets `color` to `color.text.primary` so content reads on every variant in both themes.
- **CR-4.** Surface never sets `overflow`: content stays unclipped, so a focused child's ring, drawn `focus.offset` outside it, is never cut at the edge. A caller who must clip (a scrolling panel body) does so on its own inner element.
- **CR-5.** Every variant has a `border.width.025` edge, `inset` a transparent one, so in `(forced-colors: active)`, where the system paints borders and drops shadows and translucent fills, every surface keeps a visible edge with no rule of its own.
- **CR-6.** `glass` is for a panel floating over the map. Surface has no breakpoint query, as the contract's [Media queries](README.md#media-queries) allow none: a caller whose panel fills with text on a phone chooses `opaque` there, as [Elevation](../foundations/elevation.md#surfaces) says.
- **CR-7.** Surfaces nest down the ladder: `raised` and `inset` sit inside `glass` or `opaque`, and `inset` inside `raised`. `glass` and `opaque` are never nested in another surface, and a `raised` or `inset` surface casts no shadow, since only floating panels do.

## Stories

No Penpot design yet, so the stories are named by the variant names the design will have: the `variant` value in PascalCase (the Conventions of `penpot/README.md`), and `Nested` shows the ladder together. Each `play` test reads the DOM and the accessibility tree, not the pixels.

| Story    | Shows                                                                                                                                               | `play` test                                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Raised` | `variant='raised'`, a card holding a heading, a line of text and a Button, on `color.surface.default`                                               | The root is a `<div>` with `pn-Surface` and `data-variant='raised'`, no role and no name; Tab moves straight to the Button inside it                                               |
| `Inset`  | `variant='inset'`, a box holding a line of text, on `color.surface.raised`                                                                          | `data-variant` is `inset`                                                                                                                                                          |
| `Glass`  | `variant='glass'`, a panel holding a heading and text, over a busy coloured backdrop that shows the blur                                            | `data-variant` is `glass`                                                                                                                                                          |
| `Opaque` | `variant='opaque'`, the same panel over the same backdrop                                                                                           | `data-variant` is `opaque`                                                                                                                                                         |
| `Nested` | A `glass` panel rendered as `<section aria-labelledby>` with its heading, holding a `raised` card that holds an `inset` box, over the busy backdrop | The outer root is a `region` named by its heading, keeps `pn-Surface` and `data-variant='glass'`; the inner surfaces carry `raised` and `inset`; a `ref` on each lands on its root |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                         | Don't                                                                                                                                          |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Use `glass` for a panel that floats over the map, and `opaque` for one full of text on a phone, as Elevation says.         | Use `glass` over a plain background or inside another panel: the blur has nothing to soften, and glass on glass loses its edge.                |
| Put `raised` cards and `inset` boxes inside a panel, stepping down the ladder.                                             | Nest a floating `glass` or `opaque` surface inside another surface, or add a shadow to a card with `className`: only floating panels cast one. |
| Render it as `<section>` or `<aside>` with `aria-labelledby` on its heading when the box is a region someone navigates to. | Give every card a landmark element: a screen of unnamed regions is noisier than plain boxes.                                                   |
| Use Dialog or Sheet for a panel that opens and closes over the screen, since they bring the focus, Esc and scrim.          | Build a dialog from a `glass` Surface: it would look right and trap no focus.                                                                  |
| Say a state in words or with an icon inside the surface.                                                                   | Tint a surface with a status colour through `className` to mean warning or success: colour is never alone.                                     |
| Change the padding through `className` with a `space.*` token when rows must run to the edge.                              | Set raw pixel padding, radius or colours on it, which leave the ladder and the themes behind.                                                  |

title: MapControls
