# Delay

How late or early a vehicle or departure runs, as a short figure in the delay's colour, such as "+3 min", with the same thing said in words to a screen reader.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/Delay`. Family: none. Shared parts: VisuallyHidden.

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`), so the layers below are the ones the drawing will name. Delay has no Base UI part: it is display text with no behaviour, so its root renders through Base UI's `useRender` hook (`@base-ui/react/use-render`), which gives it the `render` prop, and its inner parts are plain elements.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                          | Base UI part                                   | Class                               | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | The whole delay, one inline run of text: a `<span>` in the delay's colour                                                           | none: a `<span>` rendered by `useRender`       | `pn-Delay`                          | none            |
| `value`             | The visible figure: the signed whole minutes ("+3", "−1"), "On time", or "—" when unknown                                           | none: a plain `<span>`, no behaviour to borrow | `pn-Delay-value`                    | none            |
| `unit`              | "min", after a space, shown only after a signed figure                                                                              | none: a plain `<span>`, no behaviour to borrow | `pn-Delay-unit`                     | none            |
| `label`             | The words a screen reader hears in place of the figure: "3 min late", "1 min early", "Delay unknown". Not drawn, so no Penpot layer | none: the VisuallyHidden shared part           | `pn-VisuallyHidden`, the part's own | none            |

Delay shows a signed figure with its unit, "+3 min" late and "−1 min" early (the true minus sign), "On time" in words when on time, and "—" with no unit when unknown, as content design writes numbers: a space before units, the true minus sign for early and "—" for unknown.

Delay's one Penpot variant property is `delay`, with the values `on-time`, `slight`, `late`, `early` and `unknown`. The code map maps it to the CSS state `[data-delay]` with the same value rather than to a prop, since the component works it out from `minutes`. The variants are `OnTime`, `Slight`, `Late`, `Early` and `Unknown`, and the stories carry those names.

## Base UI parts

Delay imports no Base UI component. It uses two Base UI utilities, at the version pinned in `package.json`: `useRender` (`@base-ui/react/use-render`) for the root and `mergeProps` (`@base-ui/react/merge-props`) to merge the caller's props over its own.

| Base UI part                     | Renders  | Perron sets                                                                                                          | Passed through                                        |
| -------------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `useRender` (a hook, not a part) | `<span>` | `defaultTagName: 'span'`, `className` (`pn-Delay` first, then the caller's), `data-delay`, the children (CR-3, CR-4) | `render`, `ref`, `className`, `style`, the rest props |

Base UI already does: swapping the root element for the one `render` gives, keeping the class, data attribute and children; merging the caller's `ref` with the element's; and merging event handlers, `className` and `style` through `mergeProps`.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop here gets this description as its JSDoc. Delay takes no `children`: it writes its own figure and words. It has no `slotProps`, because the contract keys `slotProps` by inner Base UI part and Delay has none; a caller restyles it through `className` on the root.

The delay is given as `minutes: number | null`, required, in minutes (positive late, negative early, `0` on time, `null` unknown) and rounded to the nearest whole minute, not as `value` or in seconds: the contract's `value` belongs to controls with `defaultValue` and `onChange`, and the tokens, the words and the visible figure all count whole minutes.

| Name                 | Type                   | Default      | Base UI prop         | Description                                                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------ | -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `minutes`            | `number \| null`       | (required)   | none                 | The delay in minutes: positive when late, negative when early, `0` on time, `null` when no real-time data says (timetable only, no signal). Rounded to the nearest whole minute.          |
| `render`             | Base UI's `render`     |              | inherited            | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `minutesUnitLabel`   | `string`               | The locale's | none                 | Overrides "min", the unit after the figure                                                                                                                                                |
| `minutesLateLabel`   | `string`               | The locale's | none                 | Overrides "min late", heard after the number when late                                                                                                                                    |
| `minutesEarlyLabel`  | `string`               | The locale's | none                 | Overrides "min early", heard after the number when early                                                                                                                                  |
| `onTimeLabel`        | `string`               | The locale's | none                 | Overrides "On time"                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `delayUnknownLabel`  | `string`               | The locale's | none                 | Overrides "Delay unknown", heard in place of "—"                                                                                                                                          |
| `className`, `style` | React's                |              | through `mergeProps` | Reach the root; `className` is merged after `pn-Delay`                                                                                                                                    |
| `ref`                | `Ref<HTMLSpanElement>` |              | `useRender`'s `ref`  | Reaches the root element                                                                                                                                                                  |

## Tokens

Delay is not interactive, so its one design state is rest; each row's state names the `data-delay` value it applies to. Delay is not one of the contract's families, so it draws no fill, border or radius.

Delay comes in one size, set in `typography.data`, with no `size` prop; a caller who needs it larger (beside a `typography.data-lg` countdown) sets the font through `className`. `typography.data` is the role for "times, delays, counts and percentages in lists and tables", where Delay sits, and a second size can join later as a `size` prop without a break.

| Part    | State                          | Property               | Token                                                  |
| ------- | ------------------------------ | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `root`  | rest, every `data-delay`       | `font`                 | `typography.data`                                      |
| `root`  | rest, every `data-delay`       | `letter-spacing`       | `typography.data-tracking`                             |
| `root`  | rest, every `data-delay`       | `font-variant-numeric` | none: the keyword `tabular-nums`, so figures line up   |
| `root`  | rest, every `data-delay`       | `white-space`          | none: the keyword `nowrap`, so "+3 min" never breaks   |
| `root`  | rest, `data-delay='on-time'`   | `color`                | `color.transit.delay.on-time`                          |
| `root`  | rest, `data-delay='slight'`    | `color`                | `color.transit.delay.slight`                           |
| `root`  | rest, `data-delay='late'`      | `color`                | `color.transit.delay.late`                             |
| `root`  | rest, `data-delay='early'`     | `color`                | `color.transit.delay.early`                            |
| `root`  | rest, `data-delay='unknown'`   | `color`                | `color.transit.delay.unknown`                          |
| `value` | rest, every `data-delay`       | `color`                | none: inherits the root's                              |
| `unit`  | rest, `data-delay` with a unit | `color`                | none: inherits the root's                              |
| `label` | rest                           | none                   | none: the VisuallyHidden part's own styles, never seen |

The space between `value` and `unit` is a text space, as content design writes "4 min", not a gap token, so a copied delay reads "+3 min".

## Keyboard and ARIA

Delay is text: it takes no focus, and no key does anything. A caller who makes it a link or button through `render` brings that element's own keys.

| Key  | Does                               | From   |
| ---- | ---------------------------------- | ------ |
| none | Delay is not focusable or operable | Perron |

| Element            | Role                         | Accessible name from                                                            | States announced |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `root`             | none: a generic `<span>`     | Not named; its text is read in place, as part of the row or sentence it sits in | none             |
| `value` and `unit` | hidden, `aria-hidden="true"` | Not read, except "On time", which is read as shown (CR-3)                       | none             |
| `label`            | text                         | The owned strings: "3 min late", "1 min early", "Delay unknown"                 | none             |

The visible figure is `aria-hidden`, with a VisuallyHidden label saying the delay in words: the number without its sign and then "min late" or "min early" ("3 min late", "1 min early"), and "Delay unknown" in place of "—", while "On time" is read from the visible text. A screen reader reads "+3 min" as "plus 3 min" and skips or spells "—", so the ear would get less than the eye, and an `aria-label` on a role-less `<span>` is not allowed.

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the colour and sign say late, slight, early or on time; the label says "N min late" or "N min early", "On time" is read as shown, and `null` says "Delay unknown". In forced colours the colour goes, and the sign and words still carry it.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: none here; Delay is inline text.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: `minutesUnitLabel`, `minutesLateLabel`, `minutesEarlyLabel`, `onTimeLabel` and `delayUnknownLabel`.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `minutes` is a number or `null`; positive, negative, zero, fractional (rounded), `NaN` and infinite (both unknown, CR-1) all render, and a story's `play` test covers each kind.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; Delay does not animate. The visible figure is `aria-hidden` because the label speaks for it, not for animation.
- [ ] Native semantics first: a `<span>`, with no role and no ARIA beyond `aria-hidden` on the figure the label replaces.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: Delay takes no focus.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: no target; Delay is not pressed.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; Delay has no motion.

## Owned strings

Every word Delay shows or announces is its own; the caller gives only `minutes`. The number is never part of a string: it renders as its own text run beside the word, so the dictionaries stay plain strings (CR-3).

| Key            | English         | Override            | Seen or heard where                                         |
| -------------- | --------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `minutesUnit`  | "min"           | `minutesUnitLabel`  | `unit`, seen after a signed figure, "+3 min"; `aria-hidden` |
| `minutesLate`  | "min late"      | `minutesLateLabel`  | `label`, heard after the number when late: "3 min late"     |
| `minutesEarly` | "min early"     | `minutesEarlyLabel` | `label`, heard after the number when early: "1 min early"   |
| `onTime`       | "On time"       | `onTimeLabel`       | `value`, seen and heard when `minutes` rounds to `0`        |
| `delayUnknown` | "Delay unknown" | `delayUnknownLabel` | `label`, heard in place of "—" when `minutes` is `null`     |

No key in `packages/perron/src/locale/en.ts` says any of these, so all five are new, each with a JSDoc line like its neighbours.

"On time" and "Delay unknown" join the data-state and delay words table in `docs/content-design.md`, with their Danish, Swedish and Norwegian, so every screen says a delay the same way; content design says delays always use the words in that table, and its test then holds the locale files to them. "min", "min late" and "min early" stay out of it, as parts of a number's phrase rather than words a screen shows on their own.

## Component rules

- **CR-1.** Delay works out its kind from `minutes` after rounding it with `Math.round`: `null`, `NaN` or an infinite number is `unknown`; `0` (and `-0`) is `on-time`; `1` or `2` is `slight`; `3` or more is `late`; `-1` or less is `early`. Early has no slight step. These are the bounds the `color.transit.delay.*` tokens describe.
- **CR-2.** The visible figure is "+N" when late and "−N" when early, with U+2212, never a hyphen-minus, then a text space and the `minutesUnit` word in `unit`. On time, `value` is the `onTime` word and there is no `unit`. Unknown, `value` is "—" (U+2014) and there is no `unit`.
- **CR-3.** When late, early or unknown, `value` and `unit` are `aria-hidden="true"` and the VisuallyHidden `label` holds the words: the number without its sign, a space and `minutesLate` or `minutesEarly`, or `delayUnknown` alone. The number and each word are separate text runs, so `expectOwnedStrings` reads the words as dictionary values. On time, `value` is read as shown and there is no `label`.
- **CR-4.** The root always carries `data-delay` with the kind from CR-1, `on-time`, `slight`, `late`, `early` or `unknown`, and the CSS reads the colour from it, as [Tokens](#tokens) gives.
- **CR-5.** Delay takes no data state. A caller showing a timetable-only or no-signal vehicle passes `minutes={null}`, as [Data states](../foundations/data-states.md#delays) says those always show an unknown delay.
- **CR-6.** Delay is not a live region. A screen that updates delays announces changes of state in its own polite live region, as [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md) asks.
- **CR-7.** Delay composes the VisuallyHidden shared part from its folder in `packages/perron/src/`, and never draws its own hiding styles. If no earlier component has added the part yet, Delay's build adds it, as the contract's [Shared parts](README.md#shared-parts) table already describes it.
- **CR-8.** The root renders through `useRender` with `mergeProps`: Delay's own props (`className` starting with `pn-Delay`, `data-delay`, the children) win over the caller's rest props, and `minutes` and every `*Label` prop are taken out of the rest before the merge, so none reaches the DOM.

## Stories

One per variant the deferred design will draw, named as CR-1's kinds in PascalCase. Each `play` test reads the accessibility tree, not the pixels.

| Story     | Shows                                          | `play` test                                                                                                              |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `OnTime`  | `minutes={0}`, "On time" in the on-time colour | `data-delay` is `on-time`; "On time" is visible and in the accessible text; no `label`; `minutes={0.4}` renders the same |
| `Slight`  | `minutes={2}`, "+2 min"                        | `data-delay` is `slight`; "+2 min" is visible and `aria-hidden`; the accessible text is "2 min late"                     |
| `Late`    | `minutes={7}`, "+7 min"                        | `data-delay` is `late`; the accessible text is "7 min late"; `minutes={2.6}` rounds to `late` and "+3 min"               |
| `Early`   | `minutes={-1}`, "−1 min" with U+2212           | `data-delay` is `early`; the figure starts with U+2212; the accessible text is "1 min early"                             |
| `Unknown` | `minutes={null}`, "—"                          | `data-delay` is `unknown`; "—" is `aria-hidden`; the accessible text is "Delay unknown"; `NaN` renders the same          |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                             | Don't                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Pass `minutes={null}` for a timetable-only or no-signal vehicle, because no real-time data says how late it is.                | Pass `0` when the delay is unknown: "On time" claims more certainty than the data has.                                         |
| Pass the delay in minutes, and let Delay round, sign and colour it.                                                            | Format the figure yourself and put it in a Text in a delay colour: the words for the ear and the `data-delay` kind go missing. |
| Set Delay beside stronger text, such as the departure time, because `color.transit.delay.unknown` is too faint to stand alone. | Use Delay alone as a row's only content when it may be unknown: "—" in that colour misses 4.5:1 by design.                     |
| Announce a changed delay in the screen's own polite live region, once, when its kind changes.                                  | Wrap Delay in a live region that reads every minute's change: it floods the screen reader.                                     |
| Use `color.transit.severity.delay` and its label for a delay disruption on a line.                                             | Use Delay for a line's disruption: it says how late one vehicle or departure runs.                                             |

title: LineBadge
markdown:
# LineBadge

A small filled label that names one Copenhagen line, a metro, S-tog, bus or regional train, in the operator's own line colour.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/LineBadge`. Family: none. Shared parts: none.

The design is deferred (ADR 0010, `docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`), so this spec sets the layers the drawing will have: a `root` board holding one text layer, `label`.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Base UI part                                  | Class          | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | -------------- | --------------- |
| `root`              | The badge: a fixed-height box in the line's colour, with the label centred in it                                                                                                                                                             | none: a `<span>` rendered through `useRender` | `pn-LineBadge` | none            |
| `label`             | The line's short name, such as "M1", "A" or "5C", from the caller's `children`. The `label` layer is the root's own text, with no element, class or `slotProps` key of its own: the root holds the text directly, so there is no inner part. | none: the root's text                         | none           | none            |

## Base UI parts

No Base UI component: `baseUiParts` is empty in `packages/perron/components.json`, and a badge has no behaviour to borrow. The root renders through Base UI's `useRender` hook, from `@base-ui/react/use-render` at the version pinned in `packages/perron/package.json`, so the contract's `render` prop works, and the component's props are merged with `mergeProps` from `@base-ui/react/merge-props`.

| Base UI part | Renders  | Perron sets                                                                                                              | Passed through                                                                       |
| ------------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `useRender`  | `<span>` | `defaultTagName: 'span'`; `className` `pn-LineBadge` then the caller's; `data-line` from `line`; `data-size` from `size` | `render`, `ref`, `children`, `className`, `style` and every other `<span>` attribute |

Base UI already does: swapping the root element for the `render` prop, merging the caller's `ref` with the element's under React 19, and merging `className`, `style` and event handlers in `mergeProps`.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop here gets this description as its JSDoc. No slots: the badge has no inner part.

| Name        | Type                                                                                            | Default    | Base UI prop | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `line`      | `'m1' \| 'm2' \| 'm3' \| 'm4' \| 'a' \| 'b' \| 'c' \| 'e' \| 'f' \| 'h' \| 'bus' \| 'regional'` | none       | none         | The line whose colours the badge takes: a metro line (`m1` to `m4`), an S-tog line (`a` to `h`), any bus (`bus`), or any regional or Øresund train (`regional`). Required, with no default; set on the root as `data-line`. |
| `size`      | `'medium' \| 'large'`                                                                           | `'medium'` | none         | `medium` is the badge in rows and lists, `size.badge` tall; `large` is the badge in a panel's header, `size.badge-lg` tall. Both sizes set the label in `typography.badge`.                                                 |
| `children`  | `ReactNode`                                                                                     | none       | none         | The line's short name as riders know it: "M1", "A", "5C", "RE". Required: the badge never derives it from `line`, which holds no bus number.                                                                                |
| `render`    | Base UI's `render`                                                                              |            | inherited    | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.                                   |
| `className` | `string`                                                                                        |            | none         | Joined after `pn-LineBadge` on the root                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `style`     | `CSSProperties`                                                                                 |            | none         | Reaches the root                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `ref`       | `Ref<HTMLSpanElement>`                                                                          |            | none         | Reaches the root element                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

`className`, `style` and `ref` reach the root, as the contract's [Root](README.md#root) says.

## Tokens

One row per part, state and property. The badge has one design state, rest: it is never interactive (CR-2). Each `line` value sets the fill and its partner label colour, as [Semantic colours](../foundations/semantic-colours.md#line-colours) pairs them.

| Part   | State                 | Property         | Token                                                                                                                                                |
| ------ | --------------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root` | rest, `line` m1       | `background`     | `color.transit.line.m1`                                                                                                                              |
| `root` | rest, `line` m1       | `color`          | `color.transit.line-on.m1`                                                                                                                           |
| `root` | rest, `line` m2       | `background`     | `color.transit.line.m2`                                                                                                                              |
| `root` | rest, `line` m2       | `color`          | `color.transit.line-on.m2`                                                                                                                           |
| `root` | rest, `line` m3       | `background`     | `color.transit.line.m3`                                                                                                                              |
| `root` | rest, `line` m3       | `color`          | `color.transit.line-on.m3`                                                                                                                           |
| `root` | rest, `line` m4       | `background`     | `color.transit.line.m4`                                                                                                                              |
| `root` | rest, `line` m4       | `color`          | `color.transit.line-on.m4`                                                                                                                           |
| `root` | rest, `line` a        | `background`     | `color.transit.line.a`                                                                                                                               |
| `root` | rest, `line` a        | `color`          | `color.transit.line-on.a`                                                                                                                            |
| `root` | rest, `line` b        | `background`     | `color.transit.line.b`                                                                                                                               |
| `root` | rest, `line` b        | `color`          | `color.transit.line-on.b`                                                                                                                            |
| `root` | rest, `line` c        | `background`     | `color.transit.line.c`                                                                                                                               |
| `root` | rest, `line` c        | `color`          | `color.transit.line-on.c`                                                                                                                            |
| `root` | rest, `line` e        | `background`     | `color.transit.line.e`                                                                                                                               |
| `root` | rest, `line` e        | `color`          | `color.transit.line-on.e`                                                                                                                            |
| `root` | rest, `line` f        | `background`     | `color.transit.line.f`                                                                                                                               |
| `root` | rest, `line` f        | `color`          | `color.transit.line-on.f`                                                                                                                            |
| `root` | rest, `line` h        | `background`     | `color.transit.line.h`                                                                                                                               |
| `root` | rest, `line` h        | `color`          | `color.transit.line-on.h`                                                                                                                            |
| `root` | rest, `line` bus      | `background`     | `color.transit.mode.bus`                                                                                                                             |
| `root` | rest, `line` bus      | `color`          | `color.transit.mode.on-bus`                                                                                                                          |
| `root` | rest, `line` regional | `background`     | `color.transit.mode.regional`                                                                                                                        |
| `root` | rest, `line` regional | `color`          | `color.transit.mode.on-regional`                                                                                                                     |
| `root` | rest                  | `font`           | `typography.badge`                                                                                                                                   |
| `root` | rest                  | `letter-spacing` | `typography.badge-tracking`, the role's twin                                                                                                         |
| `root` | rest                  | `border-radius`  | `radius.sm`                                                                                                                                          |
| `root` | rest, `size` medium   | `height`         | `size.badge`                                                                                                                                         |
| `root` | rest, `size` large    | `height`         | `size.badge-lg`                                                                                                                                      |
| `root` | rest, `size` medium   | `min-width`      | `size.badge`, so a one-letter line is square. The badge is at least as wide as it is tall, `size.badge` or `size.badge-lg`.                          |
| `root` | rest, `size` large    | `min-width`      | `size.badge-lg`                                                                                                                                      |
| `root` | rest, `size` medium   | `padding-inline` | `space.150`, 6 px either side of a longer label such as "5C" in a 22 px badge.                                                                       |
| `root` | rest, `size` large    | `padding-inline` | `space.200`, 8 px in a 34 px badge, the same proportion as medium.                                                                                   |
| `root` | rest, forced colours  | `border`         | `border.width.025` in `transparent`, which Windows' contrast themes paint in the text colour, so the badge keeps its shape when the fill is dropped. |

## Keyboard and ARIA

No keys: the badge is not focusable and does nothing when pressed (CR-2).

| Element | Role                               | Accessible name from              | States announced |
| ------- | ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `root`  | none: a `<span>`, read as its text | Its text, the caller's `children` | none             |

The label alone is what a screen reader hears, with no owned word for the mode ("Bus", "Metro") and no `aria-label`: the label is the line's name as riders say it, the colour only repeats it, and the row the badge sits in names the rest. A `<span>` without a role can't carry `aria-label` reliably either.

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the colour names the line, and the label, which a screen reader reads, names it too, for every `line` value; `children` is required.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: none here; the badge is inline text.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: no owned strings, so no `*Label` props.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `children` renders as a string, an element and a list alike, inside the fixed-height box, on one line.
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; the badge has no motion.
- [ ] Native semantics first: a plain `<span>`, no ARIA.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: never focused; it has no tab stop.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: no target; a pressable line is the caller's button or link around the badge, which meets the minimum itself.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; the badge has no motion.

## Owned strings

No owned strings: the label is the caller's `children`, and the badge announces nothing else.

## Component rules

- **CR-1.** The root sets `data-line` and `data-size` with the props' values, the default size included, and the CSS selects on them: `.pn-LineBadge[data-line='m1']`, `.pn-LineBadge[data-size='large']`.
- **CR-2.** The badge is never interactive: no hover, focus, pressed or selected look, no tab stop, no role. A line the rider can press is a Perron button or link with the badge inside it.
- **CR-3.** The label sits on one line, centred both ways (`display: inline-flex`, `white-space: nowrap`), and the badge grows wider for a longer label; it never wraps or truncates.
- **CR-4.** The fill and the label colour are always the pair the line's tokens give, in both themes, never adjusted: `color.transit.line.<id>` with `color.transit.line-on.<id>`, `color.transit.mode.bus` with `color.transit.mode.on-bus`, `color.transit.mode.regional` with `color.transit.mode.on-regional`.
- **CR-5.** The CSS reads only the component layer's [token families](README.md#token-families), `color.transit.*` among them, and no `opacity`.
- **CR-6.** The stories of the five lines whose official pairs miss 4.5:1 (M1, M4, A, B and C, listed on [Semantic colours](../foundations/semantic-colours.md#line-colours)) turn off axe's `color-contrast` rule in their own `parameters.a11y`, with a comment citing that list, while every other story keeps it: the pairs stay exact by rule, so axe would fail them on every run.

## Stories

One per variant the deferred design will show: the Penpot properties `line` and `size`, in that order, with no `State` property, since the badge has one state. The design has these 24 variants, every `line` at both sizes, each story named `<Line><Size>` and showing that line's short name as `children`, with the metro stories titled "M1 Medium" to "M4 Large" as riders write the line. One more story, `Default`, comes first and gives the contract story its args: M2 at `medium`, a pair that meets 4.5:1, so axe's `color-contrast` rule stays on there.

| Story            | Shows                                | `play` test |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------ | ----------- |
| `Default`        | `line` m2, `size` medium, "M2"       | none        |
| `M1Medium`       | `line` m1, `size` medium, "M1"       | none        |
| `M2Medium`       | `line` m2, `size` medium, "M2"       | none        |
| `M3Medium`       | `line` m3, `size` medium, "M3"       | none        |
| `M4Medium`       | `line` m4, `size` medium, "M4"       | none        |
| `AMedium`        | `line` a, `size` medium, "A"         | none        |
| `BMedium`        | `line` b, `size` medium, "B"         | none        |
| `CMedium`        | `line` c, `size` medium, "C"         | none        |
| `EMedium`        | `line` e, `size` medium, "E"         | none        |
| `FMedium`        | `line` f, `size` medium, "F"         | none        |
| `HMedium`        | `line` h, `size` medium, "H"         | none        |
| `BusMedium`      | `line` bus, `size` medium, "5C"      | none        |
| `RegionalMedium` | `line` regional, `size` medium, "RE" | none        |
| `M1Large`        | `line` m1, `size` large, "M1"        | none        |
| `M2Large`        | `line` m2, `size` large, "M2"        | none        |
| `M3Large`        | `line` m3, `size` large, "M3"        | none        |
| `M4Large`        | `line` m4, `size` large, "M4"        | none        |
| `ALarge`         | `line` a, `size` large, "A"          | none        |
| `BLarge`         | `line` b, `size` large, "B"          | none        |
| `CLarge`         | `line` c, `size` large, "C"          | none        |
| `ELarge`         | `line` e, `size` large, "E"          | none        |
| `FLarge`         | `line` f, `size` large, "F"          | none        |
| `HLarge`         | `line` h, `size` large, "H"          | none        |
| `BusLarge`       | `line` bus, `size` large, "5C"       | none        |
| `RegionalLarge`  | `line` regional, `size` large, "RE"  | none        |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                                        | Don't                                                                                                                |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Name the line in words near the badge, such as "M1 towards Vanløse", because five official pairs (M1, M4, A, B, C) miss 4.5:1 and stay so | Rely on the badge's label alone where the line matters, such as the only mention of a line in a disruption           |
| Pass the name riders know as `children`: "5C", "A", "RE"                                                                                  | Pass a sentence or a mode word ("Bus 5C"); the colour already says the mode, and the badge is sized for a short name |
| Use a line colour as a fill only in a LineBadge, and as a dot, ring, rail or swatch elsewhere, as Semantic colours says                   | Fill another shape, such as a chip or a panel header, with a line colour                                             |
| Wrap the badge in a Perron button or link when the rider can open the line                                                                | Add `onClick` or `tabIndex` to the badge; it has no focus ring, role or target size                                  |
| Keep brand buttons out of rows of line badges                                                                                             | Put a brand button beside bus badges, where its yellow fill and ink label read as one more bus                       |
| Choose `large` only for the one badge that heads a panel                                                                                  | Mix sizes in one row or list                                                                                         |

title: SeverityLabel
markdown:
# SeverityLabel

The kind of a disruption on a line, as its icon and its name in its colour, such as a warning triangle and "Delays", heading a disruption card or a row in a list of disruptions.

## Anatomy

Penpot page `Components/SeverityLabel`, not drawn yet: the design is deferred (`docs/adr/0010-unattended-runs-with-design-deferred.md`), so this spec decides the drawing. Family: none. Shared parts: none.

SeverityLabel has no Base UI part: it is a label with no behaviour, and the registry gives it no `baseUiParts`. Its root renders through Base UI's `useRender` hook (`@base-ui/react/use-render`), which gives it the `render` prop, and its inner parts are plain elements.

| Part (Penpot layer) | What it is                                                                                                                              | Base UI part                                   | Class                    | `slotProps` key |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | --------------- |
| `root`              | The whole label, one inline run: a `<span>` laid out as an inline grid, the icon beside the name, in the kind's colour                  | none: a `<span>` rendered by `useRender`       | `pn-SeverityLabel`       | none            |
| `icon`              | The kind's icon from `packages/perron/icons/`, an inline `<svg>` drawn in `currentColor` at `icon.size.325`, hidden from screen readers | none: a plain `<svg>`, no behaviour to borrow  | `pn-SeverityLabel-icon`  | none            |
| `label`             | The kind's name, "Delays", "Diversions", "Planned works" or "Data feed problems", the words the eye and the ear both get                | none: a plain `<span>`, no behaviour to borrow | `pn-SeverityLabel-label` | none            |

The icon for each kind is the one `packages/perron/icons/icons.json` lists for it under Disruptions: `warning` for delays, `diversion` for diversions, `calendar` for planned works and `signal-off` for data feed problems. Each colour is the `color.transit.severity.*` token of the same name, which [Data states](../foundations/data-states.md#kinds-of-disruption) says always comes "with its icon and its name".

SeverityLabel's one Penpot variant property is `severity`, with the values `delay`, `data`, `diversion` and `planned`, the names of the `color.transit.severity.*` tokens. It maps to the `severity` prop with the same values. The variants are `Delay`, `Data`, `Diversion` and `Planned`, and the stories carry those names. There is no `State` property: the label is not interactive.

## Base UI parts

SeverityLabel imports no Base UI component. It uses two Base UI utilities, at the version pinned in `package.json`: `useRender` (`@base-ui/react/use-render`) for the root and `mergeProps` (`@base-ui/react/merge-props`) to merge the caller's props with its own.

| Base UI part                     | Renders  | Perron sets                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Passed through                                        |
| -------------------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `useRender` (a hook, not a part) | `<span>` | `defaultTagName: 'span'`, `state: { severity }` (which `useRender` writes as `data-severity` and passes to a `render` function), `data-severity` again in its own props so the caller's can't overwrite it (CR-6), `className` (`pn-SeverityLabel` first, then the caller's), the children: `icon` and `label` (CR-2, CR-3) | `render`, `ref`, `className`, `style`, the rest props |

Base UI already does: swapping the root element for the one `render` gives, keeping the class, the data attribute and the children; turning each `state` property into a `data-*` attribute; merging the caller's `ref` with the element's; and joining `className` and `style` and chaining event handlers through `mergeProps`.

## Props

In MUI's layout. Every prop here gets this description as its JSDoc. SeverityLabel takes no `children`: it writes its own icon and words (CR-4). It has no `slotProps`, because the contract keys `slotProps` by inner Base UI part and SeverityLabel has none; a caller restyles it through `className` on the root. `className` and `style` are React's, inherited and so not rows of the table below: both reach the root through `mergeProps`, and `className` is merged after `pn-SeverityLabel`.

The kind is `severity`, as MUI's Alert names the same idea, rather than `variant`: the contract's `variant` is a look with a default, and the kind is what the label says, so it has none.

The kind is required, with no default, and typed `'delay' | 'data' | 'diversion' | 'planned'` after the `color.transit.severity.*` tokens: a label with no kind says nothing true, and a default of `delay` would claim a delay the caller never gave.

| Name                    | Type                                            | Default      | Base UI prop        | Description                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `severity`              | `'delay' \| 'data' \| 'diversion' \| 'planned'` | (required)   | none                | The kind of disruption: `delay` for vehicles running late, `diversion` for a changed route, `planned` for planned works, `data` for a problem with the real-time data feed.               |
| `render`                | Base UI's `render`                              |              | inherited           | Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render. |
| `delaysLabel`           | `string`                                        | The locale's | none                | Overrides "Delays", the name shown for `severity='delay'`                                                                                                                                 |
| `diversionsLabel`       | `string`                                        | The locale's | none                | Overrides "Diversions", the name shown for `severity='diversion'`                                                                                                                         |
| `plannedWorksLabel`     | `string`                                        | The locale's | none                | Overrides "Planned works", the name shown for `severity='planned'`                                                                                                                        |
| `dataFeedProblemsLabel` | `string`                                        | The locale's | none                | Overrides "Data feed problems", the name shown for `severity='data'`                                                                                                                      |
| `ref`                   | `Ref<HTMLSpanElement>`                          |              | `useRender`'s `ref` | Reaches the root element                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `className`             | `string`                                        |              | none                | Joined after `pn-SeverityLabel` on the root                                                                                                                                               |
| `style`                 | `CSSProperties`                                 |              | none                | Reaches the root                                                                                                                                                                          |

## Tokens

SeverityLabel is not interactive, so its one design state is rest; each row's state names the `data-severity` value it applies to. It is not one of the contract's families, and the `color.transit.severity.*` tokens colour an "icon and label" with no tinted surface of their own, so it draws no fill, border or radius.

SeverityLabel comes in one size, with no `size` prop: set in `typography.label-sm`, with a `space.100` gap between the icon and the name and the icon at `icon.size.325`, the disruption icons' size "inline with label and caption text". `typography.label-sm` (12 px, 500) keeps the label below a card's `typography.heading-sm` title rather than competing with it; a second size can join later as a `size` prop without a break.

| Part           | State                             | Property                    | Token                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------- | --------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`         | rest, every `data-severity`       | `display`                   | none: the keyword `inline-grid`                                                                                                                                   |
| `root`         | rest, every `data-severity`       | `grid-template-columns`     | none: `auto 1fr`, the icon's column and the name's                                                                                                                |
| `root`         | rest, every `data-severity`       | `grid-template-rows`        | none: `auto 1fr`, the name's first line and the rest of its lines (CR-8)                                                                                          |
| `root`         | rest, every `data-severity`       | `align-items`               | none: the keyword `center`, so the icon sits on the middle of the first row, the name's first line (CR-8)                                                         |
| `root`         | rest, every `data-severity`       | `column-gap`                | `space.100`                                                                                                                                                       |
| `root`         | rest, every `data-severity`       | `font`                      | `typography.label-sm`                                                                                                                                             |
| `root`         | rest, every `data-severity`       | `letter-spacing`            | `typography.label-sm-tracking`                                                                                                                                    |
| `root`         | rest, every `data-severity`       | `--perron-icon-size`        | `icon.size.325`                                                                                                                                                   |
| `root`         | rest, `data-severity='delay'`     | `color`                     | `color.transit.severity.delay`                                                                                                                                    |
| `root`         | rest, `data-severity='data'`      | `color`                     | `color.transit.severity.data`                                                                                                                                     |
| `root`         | rest, `data-severity='diversion'` | `color`                     | `color.transit.severity.diversion`                                                                                                                                |
| `root`         | rest, `data-severity='planned'`   | `color`                     | `color.transit.severity.planned`                                                                                                                                  |
| `root::before` | rest, every `data-severity`       | `content`                   | none: `'\200b' / ''`, a zero-width space screen readers skip, as a strut one line of `typography.label-sm` tall, so the first row is the name's first line (CR-8) |
| `root::before` | rest, every `data-severity`       | `grid-row`, `grid-column`   | none: `1` and `1`, the icon's cell (CR-8)                                                                                                                         |
| `icon`         | rest, every `data-severity`       | `inline-size`, `block-size` | `--perron-icon-size`, through the `.perron-icon` class `perron.css` gives                                                                                         |
| `icon`         | rest, every `data-severity`       | `stroke`, `fill`            | none: `currentColor`, the root's colour                                                                                                                           |
| `icon`         | rest, every `data-severity`       | `grid-row`, `grid-column`   | none: `1` and `1`, the strut's cell, the name's first line (CR-8)                                                                                                 |
| `label`        | rest, every `data-severity`       | `color`                     | none: inherits the root's                                                                                                                                         |
| `label`        | rest, every `data-severity`       | `grid-row`, `grid-column`   | none: `1 / span 2` and `2`, both rows of the second column (CR-8)                                                                                                 |

Every `color.transit.severity.*` token reaches 4.5:1 on `color.surface.default`, `raised` and `inset` in both themes ([Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#text-on-surfaces)), so the name reads as text and the icon as a mark wherever the label sits.

## Keyboard and ARIA

SeverityLabel is text: it takes no focus, and no key does anything. A caller who makes it a link or button through `render` brings that element's own keys and must give it a target of `size.target-min`.

| Key  | Does                                       | From   |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------ | ------ |
| none | SeverityLabel is not focusable or operable | Perron |

| Element | Role                         | Accessible name from                                                                         | States announced |
| ------- | ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `root`  | none: a generic `<span>`     | Not named; its text is read in place, as part of the card or row it heads                    | none             |
| `icon`  | hidden, `aria-hidden="true"` | Not read: the `label` beside it says the same                                                | none             |
| `label` | text                         | The owned string for the kind: "Delays", "Diversions", "Planned works", "Data feed problems" | none             |

What axe won't catch, from the contract, each with how this component meets it:

- [ ] Everything the eye is told, the ear is told, for every shape each prop accepts: the colour and the icon say the kind, and the `label` says it in words for every `severity`; the icon is `aria-hidden` because the word beside it carries the same meaning. In forced colours the colour goes, and the icon and the word still carry it.
- [ ] Every landmark and named region has an accessible name: none here; SeverityLabel is inline text.
- [ ] Every default label can be overridden: `delaysLabel`, `diversionsLabel`, `plannedWorksLabel` and `dataFeedProblemsLabel`.
- [ ] Every shape the type accepts renders, in every variant: `severity` is one of four strings, and each has its story; a `*Label` string replaces only its own kind's word, and an undefined one keeps the locale's (CR-5).
- [ ] A hidden copy kept for animation is `aria-hidden`, and a collapsed region is `inert`: none here; SeverityLabel does not animate. The icon is `aria-hidden` because the word speaks for it, not for animation.
- [ ] Native semantics first: a `<span>` with a `<span>` of text and an `<svg>`, no role, and no ARIA beyond `aria-hidden` and `focusable="false"` on the icon.
- [ ] Focus moves in reading order and returns on close: SeverityLabel takes no focus.
- [ ] Every target is at least `size.target-min` square: no target; SeverityLabel is not pressed.
- [ ] Loops stop when the system asks for less motion: none here; SeverityLabel has no motion.

## Owned strings

Every word SeverityLabel shows is its own; the caller gives only `severity`. The names are the kinds of disruption as `packages/perron/icons/icons.json` and [Data states](../foundations/data-states.md#kinds-of-disruption) name them, set in sentence case.

The four names are "Delays", "Diversions", "Planned works" and "Data feed problems": the names the icons and the tokens already give, plural as names of a kind rather than of one event. They reuse the existing `delays` key, its JSDoc widened to "A line's delays: a heading, and the name of the delay kind of disruption", and add `diversions`, `plannedWorks` and `dataFeedProblems`. All four join the data-state, delay and disruption words table of `docs/content-design.md`, so every screen names a disruption the same way in all four languages.

| Key                | English              | Override                | Seen or heard where                                                          |
| ------------------ | -------------------- | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `delays`           | "Delays"             | `delaysLabel`           | `label` when `severity='delay'`, seen and read as shown; the key `en.ts` has |
| `diversions`       | "Diversions"         | `diversionsLabel`       | `label` when `severity='diversion'`, seen and read as shown; new             |
| `plannedWorks`     | "Planned works"      | `plannedWorksLabel`     | `label` when `severity='planned'`, seen and read as shown; new               |
| `dataFeedProblems` | "Data feed problems" | `dataFeedProblemsLabel` | `label` when `severity='data'`, seen and read as shown; new                  |

Each new key gets a JSDoc line like its neighbours in `packages/perron/src/locale/en.ts`, and its Danish, Swedish and Norwegian in `da.ts`, `sv.ts` and `nb.ts`.

## Component rules

- **CR-1.** Each `severity` has one icon, one colour and one word, never mixed: `delay` is `warning`, `color.transit.severity.delay` and `delays`; `diversion` is `diversion`, `color.transit.severity.diversion` and `diversions`; `planned` is `calendar`, `color.transit.severity.planned` and `plannedWorks`; `data` is `signal-off`, `color.transit.severity.data` and `dataFeedProblems`.
- **CR-2.** The root always carries `data-severity` with the `severity` value, written in SeverityLabel's own props so the caller's can't overwrite it (CR-6), besides `useRender`'s `state: { severity }`, which a `render` function receives; the CSS reads the colour from it, as [Tokens](#tokens) gives. The colour is set once, on the root; the icon and the word take it through `currentColor` and inheritance, as [Icons](../foundations/icons.md#style) says: "Set the colour on the text, never on the icon."
- **CR-3.** The `icon` is the icon file's own drawing, inlined as JSX: the file's `viewBox`, `fill`, `stroke`, `stroke-width`, `stroke-linecap` and `stroke-linejoin` and its child elements, unchanged, with no `width` or `height`, the classes `perron-icon` and `pn-SeverityLabel-icon`, `aria-hidden="true"` and `focusable="false"`. The package builds with `tsc` and has no SVG loader, and an icon redrawn by hand would drift from `packages/perron/icons/`, which the icon check holds to its grid and stroke. The `icon` comes before the `label` in reading order, so it sits on the start side in right-to-left text.
- **CR-4.** SeverityLabel takes no `children`, and its props type leaves them out: the name of each kind is the owned string, overridden on one instance by its `*Label` prop, so the words stay those of content design. A caller's own sentence about the disruption goes beside the label, not in it.
- **CR-5.** SeverityLabel reads its words with `useOwnedStrings({ delays: delaysLabel, diversions: diversionsLabel, plannedWorks: plannedWorksLabel, dataFeedProblems: dataFeedProblemsLabel })` from `packages/perron/src/PerronProvider.tsx`, and shows only the one its `severity` names.
- **CR-6.** The root renders through `useRender` with `mergeProps`: SeverityLabel's own props (`className` starting with `pn-SeverityLabel`, `data-severity`, the children) win over the caller's rest props, and `severity` and every `*Label` prop are taken out of the rest before the merge, so none reaches the DOM.
- **CR-7.** SeverityLabel is not a live region. A screen that adds or changes a disruption announces it in its own polite live region, as [Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#what-a-person-checks) asks.
- **CR-8.** The `label` never wraps between the icon and the word: the root is an `inline-grid` whose first row is one line of the name's typography, so a long translated name wraps inside `label` and the icon stays centred beside its first line, as it sits on a name of one line.

## Stories

One per variant the deferred design will draw, named as the `severity` values in PascalCase. Each `play` test reads the accessibility tree and the DOM, not the pixels.

| Story       | Shows                                                             | `play` test                                                                                                                                       |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Delay`     | `severity='delay'`: the `warning` icon and "Delays"               | `data-severity` is `delay`; the accessible text is "Delays"; the icon is `aria-hidden`; `delaysLabel="Late trains"` shows and reads "Late trains" |
| `Data`      | `severity='data'`: the `signal-off` icon and "Data feed problems" | `data-severity` is `data`; the accessible text is "Data feed problems"; the icon is `aria-hidden`                                                 |
| `Diversion` | `severity='diversion'`: the `diversion` icon and "Diversions"     | `data-severity` is `diversion`; the accessible text is "Diversions"; the icon is `aria-hidden`                                                    |
| `Planned`   | `severity='planned'`: the `calendar` icon and "Planned works"     | `data-severity` is `planned`; the accessible text is "Planned works"; the icon is `aria-hidden`                                                   |

## Do and don't

For a caller using the component, with the reason.

| Do                                                                                                                      | Don't                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Head a disruption with SeverityLabel, then say what is happening in a plain sentence beside it, as content design asks. | Let the label stand for the disruption: "Delays" says the kind, not where, why or how long.                                            |
| Use SeverityLabel wherever a kind of disruption is named, so its icon, colour and word always come together.            | Set your own text in a `color.transit.severity.*` colour, or show a disruption icon alone: colour and icons never carry meaning alone. |
| Use Delay for how late one vehicle or departure runs.                                                                   | Use SeverityLabel with `severity='delay'` for one late vehicle: it names a disruption on a line.                                       |
| Use `severity='data'` for a problem with the real-time feed across a line or the network.                               | Use it for one silent vehicle: that is the Prik's "No signal" state, said with its own word.                                           |
| Show a line running normally with the "Running normally" word, and no SeverityLabel.                                    | Invent a fifth kind, such as a neutral or success severity, for good news: the four kinds are disruptions.                             |
| Make the whole disruption card the link or button, with the label inside it.                                            | Make SeverityLabel itself a filter control through `render`: it is a label, smaller than `size.target-min`, and has no pressed state.  |
